source_issues.title: Load MCP servers asynchronously to not block startup
source_issues.evidence: exa: ~2s (OAuth discovery + connection), grep_app: ~624ms, context7: ~471ms. Users wait 2-3+ seconds before UI appears. Related issues #13672 and #8277 confirm this is a known pattern.

signals.topic: Command substitution uses wrong working directory when server and client are in different directories
signals.summary: When opencode serve is started in one directory and the web UI opens a project in a different directory, command substitution (e.g., !`git remote ls`) runs with the server's working directory instead of the client's project directory, producing incorrect output silently.
aliases: command substitution pwd wrong in web ui
serve working directory vs client project directory mismatch
signals.review_reason: Command substitution is a core feature for any project-specific context (git commands, file paths, etc.). Running with the wrong pwd silently produces incorrect results, which could lead to wrong git operations or file references. This is a high-confidence, reproducible bug in a frequently used feature.

source_issues.title: Command substitution uses wrong pwd
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided: server started in ~/projects/empty, client opened ~/projects/dir2, command substitution returned wrong pwd. Screenshot evidence attached. Root cause: server pwd used instead of client pwd.

signals.topic: Subtasks and task sub-sessions don't inherit the selected thinking level, falling back to model default
signals.summary: When a non-default thinking level is selected, command-created subtasks and task sub-sessions lose the thinking level configuration and fall back to the model default, forcing users to reconfigure thinking level for every subtask.
aliases: thinking level not inherited subtask task
signals.review_reason: Recurring UX friction: users with custom thinking configurations must repeatedly re-select their preference for every subtask. While not blocking, it creates repeated manual work that degrades the workflow efficiency of power users.

source_issues.title: Subtasks and task calls don't inherit selected thinking level
source_issues.evidence: Non-default thinking level selected, subtask/task paths lose it and use 'default'. ACP/Desktop command flows also affected. User must reconfigure thinking level for every subtask.

signals.topic: Skill creation fails with unhandled AnthropicInvalidDataException during multipart form serialization
signals.summary: 用户在使用 SDK 创建 Skill 时触发 AnthropicInvalidDataException 异常，堆栈显示 HttpRequestBodies.multipartFormData 序列化逻辑无法处理 ARRAY 类型 JsonNode，导致 create() 方法完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但 issue #306 展示了明确的用户阻断证据：核心功能 SkillService.create() 在主流程路径上完全抛出未捕获异常，堆栈路径覆盖 SDK 内部序列化层，用户在正常使用 SDK 时即可触发（非极端边界条件）。open 状态且有 5 条评论表明问题持续活跃，具有真实用户影响。归类为 P1 而非 P0 是因为单仓单 issue 无高频证据支撑，但明确属于主流程阻断的用户痛点。

source_issues.title: Unexpected JsonNode type in array: ARRAY when creating Skill
source_issues.evidence: 完整的 Java/Kotlin 堆栈跟踪，异常发生于 HttpRequestBodies.kt:130 的 serializePart 方法，触发路径为 SkillServiceImpl.create -> RetryingHttpClient.execute，5 条评论持续讨论该问题，标记为 recently_active。

signals.topic: Mid-stream SSE error events report incorrect HTTP status code (200 instead of actual error code)
signals.summary: When the API returns HTTP 200 (streaming started) but then sends an SSE error event (e.g. overloaded_error), the SDK raises APIStatusError with status_code=200 instead of the actual error code (e.g. 529). This breaks caller retry/fallback logic that depends on status codes.
aliases: SSE error event wrong status code
signals.review_reason: This is a production-critical bug: mid-stream SSE errors (e.g. overloaded_error) carry the wrong HTTP status code (200), causing caller retry/fallback logic to misfire. The evidence is explicit — pydantic-ai's FallbackModel checks status_code >= 500 but received 200, so fallback never fired. Any production system relying on status code for retry decisions is broken. Count=1 but impact is severe and spans any caller using streaming + fallback patterns.

source_issues.title: Mid-stream SSE errors get `status_code=200` instead of the actual error code
source_issues.evidence: In production with pydantic-ai's FallbackModel, which checks status_code >= 500 to decide whether to try the next model. The overloaded error had status_code=200, so fallback never fired. The SSE error type and body are correct, but status_code is wrong, breaking all callers that make retry decisions based on status code.

signals.topic: Gift subscription redeemed but account stuck on Free plan with no resolution path
signals.summary: A user redeemed a Max gift subscription over a week ago. The redemption page confirms success but the account remains on the Free plan. Support channels are inaccessible (blank page on support portal, AI bot cannot escalate to human agents). The user loses paid Max plan access for 7+ days with no available resolution.
aliases: Max plan entitlement not granted after gift redemption
signals.review_reason: This is a complete billing entitlement failure: a Max plan subscription was paid for and redeemed, confirmed by the redemption system, but the account entitlement was never applied. The user has zero resolution path (support portal blank, AI bot cannot escalate). Count=1 but represents a critical paid service failure with direct financial loss and no available workaround or support channel.

source_issues.title: Gift subscription redeemed but account stuck on Free plan – no human support available
source_issues.evidence: Account remains on Free plan 7+ days after gift redemption. Redemption page confirms 'This gift has already been redeemed'. Support portal shows blank page after login. Email support AI bot explicitly states it cannot perform backend operations or connect to human agents. No resolution path exists. This represents complete billing entitlement failure with no available support channel.

signals.topic: client.beta.files.upload fails with PathLike objects in tuple argument
signals.summary: Passing a PathLike object (e.g. Path('foo.txt')) as the second element of a tuple to client.beta.files.upload fails because the internal _transform_file function has a logic error where the first if-block catches all tuples before the second if-block that handles PathLike contents can execute.
signals.review_reason: File upload with PathLike objects is a common operation that is documented as supported but actually fails due to a control flow bug in the SDK. The SDK's own type signatures promise PathLike support but the implementation has a dead code path. This is a clear API contract violation causing workflow failure.

source_issues.title: [BUG] client.beta.files.upload PathLike error
source_issues.evidence: The file signature documents PathLike support but the implementation has a control flow bug: in _transform_file, the first if-block catches all tuples, preventing the second if-block (which handles reading PathLike contents) from ever executing. This is a straightforward code logic error causing a common upload operation to silently fail.

signals.topic: ServerToolResult content blocks not delivered when client tools interrupt the streaming turn
signals.summary: When the Messages API returns stop_reason=tool_use (requesting a client tool) while server-side tools (code_execution, web_search) are still running concurrently, the ServerToolResult content blocks for those server tools are never delivered — neither during streaming, in the final message, nor in subsequent API calls. This causes orphaned server_tool_use blocks with no matching result.
aliases: server tool result missing stream interruption
orphaned server_tool_use blocks no tool result
signals.review_reason: Server tool result delivery failure causes UX-level production impact: frontend spinners stuck in perpetual 'running' state, monitoring systems flag false failures, and applications must implement heuristic workarounds. The evidence includes production load test data across multiple users showing consistent orphaned tool blocks. This breaks a core multi-tool workflow expectation.

source_issues.title: ServerToolResult not delivered when client tools interrupt the stream (code_execution + client tool concurrency)
source_issues.evidence: Production load test evidence shows server_tool_use blocks (text_editor_code_execution, web_search) start at t=4-6s, client tool starts at t=7-14s, stream ends for client tool, but server tool results are never delivered in the response or subsequent API calls. Applications must implement heuristic cleanup to assume server tool completion at the next iteration. Frontend spinners get stuck showing 'running' forever. Monitoring/load tests flag these as failures even though operations succeeded.

signals.topic: Streaming with adaptive thinking terminates prematurely with stop_reason=terminated when tool input content exceeds ~6-8KB
signals.summary: When using streaming with adaptive thinking enabled, the API returns stop_reason=terminated when the tool input content parameter exceeds approximately 6-8KB of text. The tool execute function never runs and truncation happens at the API streaming response level. Retry produces the same result consistently.
aliases: adaptive thinking streaming truncated tool input
tool_use content size limit adaptive thinking
signals.review_reason: Adaptive thinking + streaming is a core feature combination that silently fails (no error, just stop_reason=terminated) when tool input exceeds an undocumented size threshold. The tool execute function never runs, meaning the operation fails silently with no error indication. This is a main flow failure for users combining adaptive thinking with streaming tool use.

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_use with adaptive thinking: terminated stop_reason on long tool input content
source_issues.evidence: Tool input content under ~150 lines (~5KB) consistently succeeds; over ~180 lines (~7KB) consistently fails with stop_reason=terminated. max_tokens is well above needed output size (42666). The tool execute function never runs — truncation happens at the API streaming response level. No workaround available except splitting large tool input across multiple smaller tool calls.

signals.topic: SDK strips directory paths from multipart file uploads, causing skills.versions.create() API 400 error
signals.summary: SDK's multipart form handler defaults stripFilenames=true, stripping directory paths from filenames (e.g. 'my-skill/SKILL.md' becomes 'SKILL.md'). This causes beta.skills.versions.create() to fail with a 400 'must be exactly in the top-level folder' error, while skills.create() happens to work. No working path exists without deleting and recreating the skill.
aliases: SKILL.md path stripped导致版本创建失败
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：skills.versions.create()无法正常工作，用户被迫采用删除重建的不规范workaround。虽仅1条报告，但影响明确指向核心功能(多版本管理)，且API返回400业务错误，非边缘场景。

source_issues.title: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking skills.versions.create()
source_issues.evidence: API返回400错误 'SKILL.md file must be exactly in the top-level folder.' 用户被迫通过删除重建skill来绕过，而非使用versions.create()正常更新。明确阻断skill版本更新这一主流程。

signals.topic: toolRunner container.id not propagated across iterations, blocking code execution tool use with client-side betaTools
signals.summary: toolRunner在迭代间不自动传递container.id，导致generateToolResponse()调用API时因缺少container_id而报invalid_request_error。setMessagesParams的两种workaround均失败：传对象立刻报错，传字符串则引发无限工具调用循环。两个bug互相叠加，使code_execution_20260120配合client-side betaTool的流式toolRunner场景完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：toolRunner与code_execution_20260120组合使用时完全不可用，且两个bug互相叠加导致没有任何workaround可用。标记为bug标签，场景属于官方beta特性组合。无限循环还会导致成本损失（重复API调用）。

source_issues.title: Bug: toolRunner does not propagate container.id across iterations, and setMessagesParams causes duplicate tool call loops
source_issues.evidence: 两种workaround均失败：传对象直接API报错400 'container: Input should be a valid string'；传字符串则引发无限工具调用循环，模型重复调用code_execution和calculate_sum永不终止。用户明确声明'There is currently no working path'，code_execution与betaTool组合场景完全阻断。

signals.topic: TextDecoder.decode() runtime crash on Node.js 22, forcing AWS Lambda users to downgrade runtime
signals.summary: SDK在Node.js 22环境下AWS Lambda运行时，TextDecoder.decode()因类型不匹配抛出异常 'Failed to execute decode on TextDecoder: parameter 1 is not of type ArrayBuffer'，导致所有API调用完全失败。唯一workaround是将Lambda运行时降级至Node.js 20，实质上阻止用户使用Node.js 22 LTS。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：SDK在Node.js 22 + AWS Lambda环境完全无法工作，所有API调用崩溃。用户唯一workaround是降级Node版本，实质上强制锁死技术栈版本。Node.js 22是LTS主流版本，用户群体广泛，runtime crash属于高优先级问题。

source_issues.title: TextDecoder.decode() fails on Node.js 22
source_issues.evidence: AWS Lambda runtime在Node.js 22下SDK完全崩溃，报错'Failed to execute decode on TextDecoder: parameter 1 is not of type ArrayBuffer'。用户被迫降级runtime至Node.js 20作为唯一workaround，实质上阻止用户使用Node.js 22 LTS特性。

signals.topic: Skills (slash commands) not resolved when passed to query() via SDK
signals.summary: Critical feature unavailability: user-installed skills (slash commands) do not work when invoked via SDK query(), returning 'Unknown skill' with zero cost, while identical invocation via CLI works correctly. Affects core functionality users expect parity on.
signals.review_reason: Critical feature unavailability: user-installed skills (slash commands) do not work when invoked via SDK query(), returning 'Unknown skill' with zero cost, while identical invocation via CLI works correctly. Affects core functionality users expect parity on.

source_issues.title: query() does not resolve user-installed skills (slash commands)
source_issues.evidence: Skills starting with '/' (e.g., '/eck:new-project') return 'Unknown skill' with $0.00 cost immediately. Same skills work correctly with claude CLI directly.

source_issues.title: agent-sdk use skills fail, but I can directly use the skill to return the data.
source_issues.evidence: Skills fail to return data when called via SDK but work directly. User explicitly notes 'They both use the same model, what's the difference' - critical feature unavailability via SDK.

signals.topic: SDK hangs/deadlocks after ~50 tool calls when string prompts are used with hooks enabled
signals.summary: Main workflow blocking: users cannot complete sessions with more than ~50 tool calls when using string prompts with hooks. The session deadlocks and all subsequent tool calls are denied.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: users cannot complete sessions with more than ~50 tool calls when using string prompts with hooks. The session deadlocks and all subsequent tool calls are denied.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: SDK hangs when string prompt generates more than ~50 tool calls with hooks enabled
source_issues.evidence: SDK deadlocks once internal 100 message buffer fills up after ~50 tool calls. Root cause: wait_for_result_and_end_input() blocks before receive_messages() starts for string prompts, causing channel full deadlock. Hooked tools get denied after CLI times out.

signals.topic: PostToolUse hook returning updatedMCPToolOutput causes JavaScript renderer crash (H.reduce is not a function)
signals.summary: Main workflow blocking: when using PostToolUse hooks with MCP servers, all tools crash simultaneously due to JavaScript error in renderer. Hooks execute correctly on Python side but user sees complete tool failure.
aliases: MCP server tools crash after hook
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: when using PostToolUse hooks with MCP servers, all tools crash simultaneously due to JavaScript error in renderer. Hooks execute correctly on Python side but user sees complete tool failure.

source_issues.title: PostToolUse hook updatedMCPToolOutput causes H.reduce is not a function in renderer despite correct hook output
source_issues.evidence: When PostToolUse hook returns valid updatedMCPToolOutput, renderer crashes with 'H.reduce is not a function'. All tools on MCP server fail simultaneously. Python hook executes correctly but JavaScript rendering layer crashes.

signals.topic: ExitPlanMode terminates the current SDK turn, preventing tool execution in same turn
signals.summary: Main workflow blocking: the plan-then-execute pattern is broken. Users cannot complete multi-step workflows that enter plan mode, get approval, exit, and execute actions in a single turn. Forces artificial multi-turn workaround.
aliases: no tool execution after plan mode exit
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: the plan-then-execute pattern is broken. Users cannot complete multi-step workflows that enter plan mode, get approval, exit, and execute actions in a single turn. Forces artificial multi-turn workaround.

source_issues.title: ExitPlanMode terminates the current SDK turn — no tool execution possible after exiting plan mode
source_issues.evidence: With bypassPermissions mode, calling ExitPlanMode immediately terminates the current turn. Any subsequent tool calls (Bash, Agent dispatch, etc.) in the same turn never execute. Requires separate follow-up query() to continue.

signals.topic: StructuredOutput tool enters infinite correction loop, never calling the tool
signals.summary: Main workflow blocking: StructuredOutput tool fails to execute properly and enters infinite loop outputting XML text instead of calling the tool. Runs until budget exhaustion, wasting resources and failing task completion.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: StructuredOutput tool fails to execute properly and enters infinite loop outputting XML text instead of calling the tool. Runs until budget exhaustion, wasting resources and failing task completion.

source_issues.title: StructuredOutput gets in a loop
source_issues.evidence: StructuredOutput gets stuck in a loop repeatedly outputting <StructuredOutput> XML text without actually calling the StructuredOutput tool. Loops until max budget is hit, wasting resources and failing to complete the task.

signals.topic: PermissionMode type missing 'auto' value — runtime errors and type failures for ACP integrations
signals.summary: The `PermissionMode` union type in the SDK does not include `'auto'`, which is supported by the Claude Code CLI at runtime. This causes type errors for ACP consumers and runtime failures when users set `permissions.defaultMode: "auto"` in settings.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report that PermissionMode type lacks 'auto' — one details runtime failures for ACP integrations (blocking actual permission configurations), the other describes type errors for consumers building on the ACP protocol. This blocks a real permission-mode workflow that the CLI itself supports, making it a concrete user-impact bug rather than a theoretical type gap.

source_issues.title: PermissionMode type is missing "auto" value
source_issues.evidence: Runtime error from @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp: 'Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto' because PERMISSION_MODE_ALIASES map is typed against PermissionMode and cannot safely include 'auto' without a cast. Users who set 'auto' in ~/.claude/settings.json get runtime failures.

source_issues.title: `PermissionMode` type missing `'auto'` value in v0.2.90
source_issues.evidence: Consumers building ACP integrations cannot pass 'auto' to setPermissionMode() or include it in mode lists without a type cast, even though the CLI itself supports it. Both runtime array (EXTERNAL_PERMISSION_MODES) and type definition are missing 'auto'.

signals.topic: Type incompatibility when @anthropic-ai/sdk >= 0.82.0 is hoisted alongside claude-agent-sdk
signals.summary: When a newer version of @anthropic-ai/sdk is installed alongside claude-agent-sdk, TypeScript produces type errors because the bundled .d.ts files are built against an older SDK version with different union types, causing ContentBlockParam mismatches at compile time.
aliases: ContentBlockParam union type incompatibility across SDK versions
signals.review_reason: Explicitly documented with a full reproduction (package.json + override + TypeScript error output). Root cause (bundled types built against ^0.74.0 vs. hoisted 0.82.0) is clearly identified. References two prior issues (#179, #121) confirming this is a recurring pattern, not a one-off. Blocks any consumer who needs both SDKs at mismatched versions from compiling their TypeScript code.

source_issues.title: Type incompatibility when @anthropic-ai/sdk >= 0.82.0 is installed alongside claude-agent-sdk
source_issues.evidence: Type error: 'ContentBlockParam' is not assignable to type 'ContentBlockParam' — ToolReferenceBlockParam not included in bundled 0.74.x types. Any code passing ContentBlockParam[] from the hoisted 0.82.0 SDK into agent SDK functions fails to compile. Referenced related issues #179 and #121 showing this is a recurring, known problem.

signals.topic: Sandbox mode silently falls back to unsandboxed execution when bubblewrap is not installed
signals.summary: When sandbox.enabled: true is set but bwrap/socat are missing, the SDK silently proceeds with full filesystem/network access with no error or warning, giving callers a false sense of security.
aliases: sandbox.enabled true silently bypassed without bubblewrap
signals.review_reason: Security-relevant bug: users who explicitly configure sandbox.filesystem and sandbox.network restrictions get zero enforcement with no feedback. The checkDependencies() path detects the failure but the error is swallowed. This defeats the entire purpose of the sandbox feature and could lead to unintended filesystem/network exposure in production environments. The issue includes a full root-cause analysis confirming no error or warning is emitted.

source_issues.title: sandbox.enabled: true silently degrades to unsandboxed execution when bubblewrap is not installed
source_issues.evidence: checkDependencies() detects missing bwrap, isSandboxingEnabled() returns false, wrapWithSandbox() short-circuits — Bash commands execute with full filesystem and network access. Caller receives no error, warning, or stream indication. allowUnsandboxedCommands: false has no effect because the per-command check is never reached. Demonstrates false sense of security for callers explicitly opting into sandboxing.

signals.topic: query() hangs indefinitely when CLI subprocess fails to start (ENOENT or missing env)
signals.summary: When the Claude Code CLI subprocess fails to start due to missing executable or cleared PATH, query() hangs forever without throwing an error or timing out, making it impossible to detect failures programmatically without external setTimeout wrappers.
aliases: query() hangs on subprocess spawn failure
ENOENT causes query() to hang forever
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: query() is the primary entry point for the SDK, and when it hangs silently on an easily-encountered failure condition (missing PATH in env, nonexistent executable), the entire application blocks with no error signal. This is a developer experience and reliability issue that makes production deployments fragile. The bug is closed with a fix merged on 2026-04-02.

source_issues.title: query() hangs forever when CLI subprocess fails to start (ENOENT / missing env)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on SDK 0.2.86 with Bun 1.3.11 and Node.js 22 on Linux (Docker debian:bookworm-slim). Root cause: spawn() ENOENT creates pipe but child never runs, readline loop blocks forever. The process.on('error') handler sets exitError but waitForExit() is never reached. stderr callback is never called. External setTimeout wrapper is the only workaround.

signals.topic: File-based agents from .claude/agents/ not discovered as invocable subagent types in SDK mode (regression 0.2.87+)
signals.summary: File-based agent definitions in .claude/agents/ are not registered as callable subagent types when using query() with settingSources, causing the Agent tool to fall back to general-purpose agents instead of using the configured model, tools, and skills of the file-based agent.
aliases: File-based subagents not discoverable via Agent tool
.claude/agents/ files not registered as subagent_type in SDK query()
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression across three consecutive versions (0.2.87-0.2.89) with a clean before/after on 0.2.85. This breaks the multi-agent orchestration workflow — the primary use case for subagent features. The agent content loads correctly but the critical Agent tool lookup fails, forcing the model to use generic fallbacks instead of the properly configured specialized agents. High impact on the intended SDK usage pattern.

source_issues.title: File-based agents from .claude/agents/ not discovered as invocable subagent types (regression since ~0.2.87)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced consistently on 0.2.87, 0.2.88, and 0.2.89. Works correctly on 0.2.85. Agent definition IS loaded into context but NOT registered as a callable subagent type in the Agent tool. Model falls back to ad-hoc general-purpose agents, bypassing the file-based agent's configured model (haiku), tools, and skills. Impacts multi-agent orchestration workflows.

signals.topic: Config restore from base branch fails on repositories with non-main default branch
signals.summary: The action hardcodes 'main' as the fallback base branch in multiple locations (agent mode, run.ts, update-comment-link.ts). On repos with 'master' or other default branches, 'git fetch origin main' fails with 'couldn't find remote ref main', breaking the config restore step for both pull_request and issue_comment events.
aliases: hardcoded main branch git fetch fails
signals.review_reason: Any repository not using 'main' as the default branch has the config restore step fail on every run. This is a persistent bug across both issue_comment and pull_request events, affecting a significant portion of repositories that still use 'master' or other branch names as default.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase fails on issue_comment events when default branch is not main
source_issues.evidence: For issue_comment events on PRs, restoreBase defaults to 'main' via agent mode instead of using the PR's actual base branch. git fetch origin main --depth=1 fails with 'couldn't find remote ref main'. The fix already exists in branch.ts using octokit.rest.repos.get to get default_branch.

source_issues.title: restoreConfigFromBase fails on repos with non-main default branch
source_issues.evidence: Hardcoded 'main' fallback in agent/index.ts (~lines 89, 96), run.ts (~line 315), update-comment-link.ts (~line 256). Fix pattern already implemented in branch.ts: octokits.rest.repos.get({owner, repo}).data.default_branch. Workaround requires setting base_branch input explicitly.

signals.topic: MCP_TIMEOUT environment variable not propagated to Claude CLI subprocess — npx-based MCP servers always fail with 30s timeout
signals.summary: The action's entrypoint does not forward MCP_TIMEOUT to the spawned Claude CLI process, causing all npx-based MCP servers to fail because 30s is insufficient for npx to download and initialize packages. Users must pre-install all MCP servers globally, adding 35-40 seconds to every workflow run.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (MCP servers via npx) is completely broken by design — the environment variable cannot be set through any user-accessible mechanism. Adds 35-40s overhead to every run as a workaround. This is a main-flow blocking issue for any user relying on npx-based MCP servers.

source_issues.title: MCP_TIMEOUT not passed to Claude CLI subprocess — npx-based MCP servers always fail
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: action's entrypoint (bun run src/entrypoints/run.ts) doesn't propagate MCP_TIMEOUT to subprocess. All 4 attempted methods (step env, settings input, GITHUB_ENV, project settings.json) are ignored. Workaround of pre-installing all MCP servers adds 35-40s to every run.

signals.topic: v2.1.89 regression: excessive permission denials cause reviews to never complete, burning turns and budget without posting results
signals.summary: After upgrading from v2.1.87 to v2.1.89, Claude enters permission-denial loops during code reviews. Runs report 5-17 permission denials, 33-41 turns, and $0.31-$1.04 in costs, yet the review never posts. The action shows a green check despite total failure.
signals.review_reason: Main code review workflow is completely blocked — reviews never complete, cost escalates (up to $1.04 per failed run), and results never post. Clear regression between versions with quantified impact (5-17 denials, 33-41 turns). High user cost in both money and CI time.

source_issues.title: v2.1.89 regression: permission denials prevent reviews from completing
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v2.1.87 to v2.1.89. Two runs show 5-17 permission denials, 15-41 turns, $0.31-$1.04 cost, 0 reviews posted. Same workflow config, only version changed. Pinning to 88c168b (v2.1.87) resolves the issue. Action reports is_error:false despite 17 denials.

signals.topic: Grep tool fails with EACCES permission denied on vendored ripgrep binary after bun install --production
signals.summary: When the action is used with bun install --production, the vendored ripgrep binary loses its executable permission, causing Grep tool calls to fail with EACCES. This is especially disruptive in workflows where Bash is restricted to scoped commands and no shell fallback is available.
signals.review_reason: Grep is a core tool in allowedTools configurations. Failure with EACCES makes the tool completely unusable. In restricted-tool workflows (where Bash is limited to scoped commands), there is no fallback, making this a main-flow block.

source_issues.title: Grep tool fails with EACCES on vendored ripgrep after bun install --production
source_issues.evidence: After bun install --production installs @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.2.89, the vendored ripgrep binary at node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/vendor/ripgrep/x64-linux/rg loses execute permissions. Grep tool fails with EACCES on every call. Workaround requires chmod +x on the binary. Action SHA bee87b3258c251f9279e5371b0cc3660f37f3f77, Bun 1.3.6.

signals.topic: git fetch authentication failure after PR #1132: GH_TOKEN stripped by subprocess env scrub, breaking credential helper
signals.summary: After PR #1132, when allowed_non_write_users is configured, the action sets GH_TOKEN in the Node process for the credential helper, but CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 (auto-enabled by the same condition) strips GH_TOKEN from subprocess environments, causing git fetch to fail with 'Authentication failed'.
aliases: git fetch credential helper auth failure
subprocess env scrub breaks git auth
signals.review_reason: The action cannot perform its most basic operation (git fetch to restore .claude config) for any user of allowed_non_write_users. This is a complete workflow block introduced by a specific PR (#1132) with a clear root cause. Users must pin to an older commit as a workaround.

source_issues.title: git fetch auth failure after #1132: credential helper's GH_TOKEN stripped by subprocess env scrub
source_issues.evidence: PR #1132 (commit 32156b1) introduced a credential helper that reads GH_TOKEN at auth time, but also auto-sets CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 which removes GH_TOKEN from subprocess environments. git fetch via credential helper fails with 'fatal: Authentication failed'. Pinning to parent commit 7225f04 resolves. Affects all repos using allowed_non_write_users != ''.

signals.topic: Gmail MCP integration fails to load in Claude Code CLI (search broken, cloud-connected MCP not injected)
signals.summary: Gmail MCP integration connected via claude.ai does not load in Claude Code CLI sessions, while Google Calendar MCP (connected identically) works fine. gmail_search_messages ignores query parameter entirely and always returns the 20 most recent emails regardless of search terms. Two separate issues: (1) MCP not injecting into CLI, (2) query parameter ignored. Affects macOS.
signals.review_reason: Gmail MCP is a key productivity integration used via claude.ai cloud connection. Two compounding failures: (1) MCP not loading in CLI means Gmail tools are completely unavailable in the terminal workflow, (2) search_messages ignoring the query parameter means even when the MCP loads, the core functionality is broken. Both are verified regressions. Note: #42793 was labeled 'invalid' by triagers but the bug description is clear and specific with a verifiable API response pattern. Keeping both under the same theme as they both block Gmail MCP usage.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Gmail MCP: search_messages ignores query parameter, always returns most recent emails
source_issues.evidence: gmail_search_messages always returns the same ~20 most recent emails regardless of query. resultSizeEstimate always 201, nextPageToken always identical. Query parameter entirely bypassed. Affects macOS users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Gmail MCP integration (gmail.mcp.claude.com) not loading in Claude Code CLI despite being connected on claude.ai
source_issues.evidence: Gmail MCP tools absent from Claude Code CLI. settings.json mcpServers is empty {} confirming cloud account injection. Google Calendar MCP (connected identically) loads and works. gmail.mcp.claude.com not reaching CLI despite claude.ai working. Marked as regression — worked in previous version.

signals.topic: Claude Cowork workspace creation fails (virtiofs mount conflict and VM connection timeout)
signals.summary: Cowork workspace fails to start on both macOS and Windows. On macOS, virtiofs mount fails when 'Documents' exists as a file (not directory) in the virtual root, blocking mkdir -p. On Windows, VM connection times out after 60 seconds even after full reinstall and AppData wipe. Cowork is entirely unusable for affected users.
signals.review_reason: Cowork is a premium product feature. Both issues render the product entirely unusable with no effective workaround. The macOS virtiofs issue is clearly documented with reproducible steps and a has repro label. The Windows VM timeout persists through full reinstall and AppData wipe — despite the 'invalid' label, the user has exhausted all standard remedies and the product is non-functional. Both are mainflow-blocking for Cowork users.

source_issues.title: Cowork: virtiofs mount fails when 'Documents' exists as file in virtual root
source_issues.evidence: virtiofs mount error: mkdir /mnt/.virtiofs-root/shared/Documents: file exists. 'Documents' as a file (not directory) in virtual root blocks Cowork project creation. Reproducible on macOS Darwin 25.3.0. Partial workaround: removing spaces from folder names helps but doesn't fix root cause.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cowork 'VM connection timeout after 60 seconds' — persists after reinstall, AppData wipe, and fresh install on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Cowork VM times out after 60 seconds. Error persists after: restart, computer restart, in-app reinstall, manual AppData deletion, full uninstall and reinstall. Windows 11, Claude Desktop app. All standard troubleshooting exhausted. Marked invalid but the workaround evidence shows this is a real unresolvable user impact.

signals.topic: Model quality regression in complex engineering workflows causing edit-without-reading behavior and thrashing
signals.summary: Since February 2026, thinking token reduction has caused a measurable collapse in model quality: Read:Edit ratio dropped from 6.6 to 2.0, users report 173 stop-hook violations per day, model edits without reading files, prematurely stops, and admits its own output is 'lazy and wrong'. Affects all platforms; power users running multi-agent workflows report 80x increase in API requests for same work output.
aliases: Thinking token reduction causing poor output
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 mainflow-blocking issue. The reporter provides quantitative evidence across 234,760 tool calls, 18,000+ prompts, and 6,852 session files. The model quality regression is evidenced by: (1) Read:Edit ratio collapse from 6.6 to 2.0 meaning the model edits without reading, (2) 173 stop-hook violations in 17 days vs 0 before, (3) 12x increase in user correction interrupts, (4) the model itself admitting 'lazy and wrong' output. This is NOT a feature request — it is a confirmed behavioral regression in complex engineering workflows that makes Claude Code unsuitable for its core use case.

source_issues.title: [MODEL] Claude Code is unusable for complex engineering tasks with the Feb updates
source_issues.evidence: Deep regression reported with quantitative data: Read:Edit ratio collapsed from 6.6 to 2.0 (70% reduction in research before edits), thinking depth dropped 73%, 173 stop-hook violations in 17 days (zero before Mar 8), 12x increase in user interrupt rate, model self-admitting 'lazy and wrong' output. API request volume increased 80x for same work output. All platforms affected. Labeled as bug by reporter with area:model tag.

signals.topic: Frequent silent session crashes on Windows (8+ crashes/day, startup deaths and mid-session drops)
signals.summary: Claude Code sessions crash silently multiple times per day on Windows 11 with no error output. Two crash types observed: startup deaths within 6-28 seconds (completing 0 turns), and mid-session drops after 1.9-14 minutes of active work. 8 crashes logged in ~4 hours. Ruled out: memory, disk, GPU, network. Affects automation and interactive use alike.
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 mainflow-blocking issue. Session crashes silently 8+ times per day with zero error output, making Claude Code unreliable for both interactive and automated workflows on Windows. The evidence includes instrumented lifecycle logging (JSONL) with crash timestamps, session lifetimes, and crash types. Memory, disk, GPU, and network have all been ruled out as root causes, pointing to a process-level bug. The 'silent death' pattern — no error output, no graceful shutdown — means users cannot diagnose or recover without external watchdog infrastructure.

source_issues.title: Frequent session crashes on Windows (8 crashes/day, startup deaths + mid-session drops)
source_issues.evidence: 8 documented crashes in ~4 hours on Windows 11 Pro. Two crash types: startup death (0 turns, 6-28s life) and mid-session drop (1.9-14min of active work). All standard diagnostics ruled out (memory: 206GB free, disk: 2.2TB free, no BSOD, no Crashpad). Instrumented via SessionStart/Stop/SessionEnd hooks with JSONL logging. Affects both interactive sessions and automation (claude -p). Reproducible daily since v2.1.90.

signals.topic: Auto-mode bypasses permissions.ask configuration, allowing unintended tool execution
signals.summary: In auto-mode, permissions.ask is ignored while permissions.allow and permissions.deny are respected. Users who configure auto-mode to prompt for specific permissions find those prompts are silently suppressed, leading to unintended code execution. Users must empty the permissions.ask array as a workaround. Affects macOS.
signals.review_reason: Auto-mode bypassing permissions.ask is a permission-safety issue. While not labeled 'security', it represents a permission model inconsistency where the allow/deny lists are respected but ask is not, creating unexpected tool execution in a mode users expect to be controlled. The workaround (emptying permissions.ask) is unintuitive and the inconsistent behavior violates user expectations about the permission model. This is an experience and safety concern, not purely a feature gap.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Auto-mode ignores permissions.ask
source_issues.evidence: permissions.ask setting ignored in auto-mode while permissions.allow and permissions.deny are respected. User-configured permission prompts are silently suppressed, allowing unintended tool execution. Workaround requires emptying the permissions.ask array. macOS platform. No working version — this never worked.

signals.topic: Claude Code agent configuration errors causing unexpected financial costs during autonomous operation
signals.summary: A user reported ~$38-45 USD in financial damage caused by Claude Code agent (Opus 4.6) making repeated configuration errors during a Kaggle competition, resulting in unintended API usage and billing charges.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed user pain point with explicit financial damage evidence (~$38-45 USD in unexpected API billing charges). The root cause — agent configuration errors during autonomous operation — represents a scenario where users lose money due to uncontrolled AI agent behavior. This aligns with the pain point definition of '明显成本损失' (obvious cost loss) and is not a generic security vulnerability or maintenance item.

source_issues.title: [SUPPORT] Financial damage report - Claude Code agent errors cost ~$45 USD
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reported ~$38-45 USD in direct financial losses caused by a Claude Code Opus 4.6 agent making repeated configuration errors during a Kaggle competition. The issue is framed as a billing/support escalation with confirmed monetary damage.

signals.topic: Discord plugin: DM reply/interaction failures due to recipientId cache expiry or partial channel state
signals.summary: Discord plugin's DM channel reply and interaction functions fail intermittently because recipientId becomes null when discord.js v14's partial channel cache is evicted. This causes 'channel is not allowlisted' errors even when the user is properly configured, breaking the core Discord messaging workflow.
aliases: Discord DM recipientId null cache expiry
Discord DM channel not allowlisted intermittent failure
signals.review_reason: Three independent issues from different users all describe the same root cause: Discord.js partial channel cache causes recipientId to be null/undefined, breaking the allowFrom check. The core Discord messaging workflow (receiving and replying to DMs) fails intermittently (~50% failure rate) even when the user is properly configured. This is a main workflow blocking issue for Discord channel users.

source_issues.title: Discord plugin: intermittent 'channel is not allowlisted' on DM replies
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with exact error message, reproduction steps, and root cause analysis. Failure rate ~50%. Root cause: DMChannel.recipientId is null after cache eviction, causing Array.includes(null) to always fail.

source_issues.title: [BUG] fetchAllowedChannel() fails for DM channels when recipientId is undefined due to partial cache
source_issues.evidence: Root cause analysis showing mutually exclusive if/else branches in fetchAllowedChannel() cause the DM path to fail when recipientId is undefined and never fall through to the groups check. Causes intermittent 'not allowlisted' error even for properly configured channels.

source_issues.title: Discord plugin: DM reply fails intermittently due to recipientId cache expiry
source_issues.evidence: Third report of same root cause: recipientId cache expiry causing DM reply failures. Independent confirmation of the bug pattern.

signals.topic: Published plugins not appearing in CLI marketplace, causing installation failures
signals.summary: Multiple plugins (specrails, ru-text) passed automated security scanning and received 'Published' status on the web dashboard but are not discoverable or installable via 'claude plugin install'. The marketplace.json in the official repo is missing their entries, and the external_plugins/ directory is missing source files for the Telegram plugin.
aliases: Plugin published but not in marketplace
Plugin install fails source path does not exist
Plugin not discoverable via CLI after publishing
signals.review_reason: Two independent plugin publishers whose plugins show 'Published' status but cannot be installed via CLI — the core value proposition of the plugin marketplace. This breaks the plugin discovery and installation workflow. The Telegram plugin source files being missing from the repository further indicates a broken packaging/release process for the official marketplace.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin source files missing from external_plugins/telegram
source_issues.evidence: Exact reproduction steps: marketplace.json references ./external_plugins/telegram but the directory does not exist. Running 'plugin install telegram@claude-plugins-official' fails with 'Source path does not exist'. Confirmed on Claude Code v2.1.90.

source_issues.title: SpecRails Plugin
source_issues.evidence: Plugin 'specrails' is 'Published' on claude.ai dashboard but 'plugin install specrails' returns 'not found in any configured marketplace'. The plugin directory is absent from ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/ despite submission on 2026-03-28.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: duplicate polling processes causing ~50% of inbound messages to be silently dropped
signals.summary: A single Claude Code session loads two .mcp.json files for the Telegram plugin (from cache and marketplace source directories), spawning two competing bun processes with long polling on the same bot token. Telegram delivers each update to one poller at random, so ~50% of inbound messages are consumed by the wrong process and never reach the Claude Code session.
signals.review_reason: The Telegram plugin's core messaging workflow silently drops ~50% of inbound messages due to two competing polling processes spawned from duplicate .mcp.json loading. Messages are consumed but never delivered to Claude Code — no error shown to user, just silent loss. This is a critical messaging workflow failure that makes the Telegram channel unreliable for any serious use.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: single session spawns two polling processes (marketplace + cache .mcp.json both loaded)
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis with process IDs, exact reproduction steps, and evidence that Telegram's getUpdates delivers each update to only one consumer. ~50% of messages are silently lost. Workaround involves manually disabling one .mcp.json file.

signals.topic: Hookify plugin: JSON parse error on Windows due to backslash in file paths on every Stop hook
signals.summary: Hookify's Stop hook throws 'Invalid \escape' JSON parse errors on every invocation on Windows because file paths containing backslashes (e.g., C:\Users\...) produce invalid JSON escape sequences when passed via stdin. The error is displayed to the user on every Claude Code session stop event.
aliases: Hookify Windows backslash JSON parse error
signals.review_reason: Hookify is a workflow-embedded tool that runs on every Claude Code session stop. On Windows, every single stop event produces a visible JSON parse error to the user — a persistent UX degradation across all hookified workflows. While not a crash, it pollutes the user's terminal output on every interaction end and undermines trust in the tool.

source_issues.title: Hookify: Invalid \escape JSON parse error on Windows (backslash in file paths)
source_issues.evidence: Exact error message and root cause: json.load(sys.stdin) fails when Windows file paths with backslashes appear in the JSON payload. Error occurs on every Stop hook invocation. Reproduction requires any Windows username with common letters. Multiple hook files affected (stop.py, pretooluse.py, posttooluse.py, userpromptsubmit.py).

signals.topic: iMessage plugin: permission relay prompts sent to self-chat instead of originating sender, breaking headless/server deployments
signals.summary: iMessage plugin sends permission relay prompts exclusively to self-chat (the server Mac's own iMessage), which is invisible to the remote user controlling Claude Code from their iPhone. This breaks the primary use case of running Claude Code headlessly on a dedicated Mac Mini with iPhone as the interface.
aliases: iMessage headless permission prompts not visible
signals.review_reason: iMessage plugin is designed for headless/server deployments, which is a core use case. Permission relay prompts vanishing into self-chat makes the plugin unusable in this configuration — users must approve via terminal or switch to Telegram. This is a main workflow blocking issue for headless Claude Code deployments using iMessage as the primary channel.

source_issues.title: Feature Request: iMessage channel plugin permission relay should support sending to allowlisted sender, not only self-chat
source_issues.evidence: Described as 'breaks the primary use case for headless/server deployments.' The issue explicitly states 'permission request effectively vanishes' because remote user cannot see self-chat on server Mac. Telegram plugin does not have this limitation. Specific environment: Mac Mini running Claude Code headless, user on iPhone, permission prompts sent to server's self-chat which is invisible to iPhone user.

signals.topic: Claude Code agent causes uncontrolled token consumption and financial loss to subscribers
signals.summary: Claude Code agent runs out of control or causes runaway token usage, resulting in significant unexpected charges to subscribers. Users report financial damage without an obvious way to prevent it.
aliases: agent runaway token burn financial damage
signals.review_reason: Clear financial damage: ~$45 USD unexpectedly charged to a Max subscriber. While evidence is thin (support escalation style), the monetary impact and cross-reference to claude-code repo confirm a real user-facing billing issue. Suggests lack of spending guardrails or runaway loop protection in Claude Code agent execution.

source_issues.title: [SUPPORT] Financial damage report - Claude Code agent ~$45 USD
source_issues.evidence: ~45 USD financial damage to a Max subscriber caused by Claude Code Opus 4.6. Escalated to support/billing team. Cross-posted to claude-code repo as issue #42329.

source_issues.title: Financial damage report - Claude Code agent ~$45 USD (cross-ref: claude-quickstarts#386)
source_issues.evidence: ~45 USD financial damage to subscriber from uncontrolled Claude Code agent behavior. Indicates lack of spending guardrails or runaway loop protection.

signals.topic: iMessage bridge echoes outbound messages as inbound, causing duplicate agent responses and significant token burn
signals.summary: When the iMessage bridge sends outbound messages (e.g., via gateway config.patch notes), it re-ingests them as inbound because the isSamePhone logic does not check the isFromMe flag. This causes the agent to respond to its own messages, burning large amounts of tokens in echo loops.
aliases: isFromMe flag not checked in isSamePhone path
signals.review_reason: Clear financial impact: ~8% weekly Opus quota burned in 30 minutes (~78k tokens). Workflow is disrupted (agent responds to its own messages). Root cause identified (isFromMe not checked in isSamePhone path). User had to implement a workaround (move to webchat). This is a recurring runtime issue with measurable cost.

source_issues.title: iMessage echo bug: isFromMe + isSamePhone messages not filtered
source_issues.evidence: Burning ~8% weekly Opus quota in 30 minutes; 78k tokens consumed across 3 API calls responding to own messages. Workaround required moving cron deliveries from iMessage to webchat. isFromMe flag is correctly set by imsg CLI but not checked by OC when isSamePhone is true.

signals.topic: Course instructions for MCP Playwright setup missing critical steps, causing silent failures for students
signals.summary: The 'MCP Servers with Claude Code' course section only provides the `claude mcp add` command but omits three essential steps: installing Playwright browsers (`npx playwright install`), installing OS-level dependencies (`sudo npx playwright install-deps`), and restarting Claude Code. Students experience silent failures where MCP tools never appear, blocking the learning workflow. Additionally, on Ubuntu 25.x, `install-deps` fails due to hardcoded old package names.
aliases: Playwright MCP silent failure in course instructions
signals.review_reason: This is a documented course instructional defect. Students following the official instructions experience silent failures where MCP Playwright tools never appear, blocking the hands-on learning workflow. The issue provides specific technical evidence of missing steps and a confirmed OS compatibility problem on Ubuntu 25.x.

source_issues.title: Claude Code in Action: MCP Playwright setup instructions missing critical steps
source_issues.evidence: Course instructions only show `claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest` without the three required steps. Students get silent failures where Playwright MCP tools never appear in Claude Code, blocking the learning exercise. Confirmed on Ubuntu 25.x with Playwright MCP v0.0.68.

signals.topic: Claude Code agent causing unexpected financial charges (~$45 USD)
signals.summary: A Max subscriber reports ~$45 USD in unexpected charges attributed to a Claude Code Opus 4.6 agent run. Issue is cross-posted from claude-code repository as a billing/financial damage escalation.
aliases: Unexpected API costs from Claude Code agent
signals.review_reason: Real financial damage ($45) reported by a subscriber with direct attribution to Claude Code agent behavior. Even without root-cause detail in this repo, the financial impact to a paying customer is a genuine user pain point warranting tracking. Kept at P1 rather than P0 because it is a single-occurrence report without confirmed root cause or remediation.

source_issues.title: [SUPPORT] Financial damage report - Claude Code agent ~$45 USD
source_issues.evidence: Max subscriber reports ~$45 USD financial damage caused by Claude Code Opus 4.6 agent run. Escalated as a support/billing issue with zero comments and no resolution as of filing.

signals.topic: Code Mode V8 OOM crash on macOS Tahoe blocks tool execution
signals.summary: Code Mode consistently crashes with V8 FatalProcessOutOfMemory on macOS 26 (Tahoe) during V8 isolate initialization, making the feature completely unusable for affected users.
aliases: Code Mode crash V8 OOM macOS
signals.review_reason: Key feature (Code Mode) completely crashes and is unusable. 100% reproducible starting v1.29, 6 identical crash reports, full stack trace provided. This blocks the primary workflow of users relying on code execution.

source_issues.title: Code Mode crashes with V8 OOM on macOS 26 (Tahoe) — Heap::SetUp fails on isolate init
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible crash with SIGTRAP/EXC_BREAKPOINT during V8 isolate init on macOS 26, 6 identical crash reports, heap setup failure, v1.29 regression, workaround requires disabling Code Mode entirely

signals.topic: VS Code extension hardcodes gpt-4o-mini model ignoring GOOSE_MODEL env var
signals.summary: The Goose VS Code extension ignores GOOSE_MODEL and OPENAI_HOST environment variables, always sending hardcoded gpt-4o-mini as the model, causing BadRequestError for custom OpenAI-compatible providers.
aliases: Extension ignores env var model config
signals.review_reason: VS Code extension ignores all model configuration, causing BadRequestError for custom provider users. The CLI works correctly but the extension completely bypasses environment variables. This breaks the main usage flow for any custom OpenAI-compatible provider.

source_issues.title: VS Code extension ignores GOOSE_MODEL env var, sends hardcoded gpt-4o-mini to custom provider
source_issues.evidence: Extension hardcodes gpt-4o-mini instead of respecting GOOSE_MODEL/OPENAI_HOST, causes BadRequestError: model does not exist on custom providers. CLI works correctly but VS Code extension ignores all model config.

signals.topic: Tetrate Agent Router OAuth returns 500 on login blocking onboarding
signals.summary: Login via Tetrate Agent Router OAuth consistently fails with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error, preventing users from completing the onboarding/login flow.
signals.review_reason: OAuth login with Tetrate Agent Router is completely broken with 500 error. This blocks the onboarding flow for users who want to use this provider. Reported as reproducible across multiple devices.

source_issues.title: Tetrate Agent Router returns 500 on Oauth
source_issues.evidence: OAuth login flow fails with 500 on Tetrate Agent Router, tested across multiple devices, blocks the onboarding/sign-in flow entirely.

signals.topic: Azure OpenAI API api-version query parameter breaks with new API version
signals.summary: New Azure OpenAI API no longer accepts api-version as a query parameter, causing Bad Request 400 errors. Goose does not respect when AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION is unset, resulting in failed API calls.
signals.review_reason: Azure OpenAI provider is completely unusable with the new API version due to rejected api-version parameter, resulting in 400 errors. This blocks all Azure OpenAI users on the new API.

source_issues.title: New version of Azure OpenAI API does not allow api-version query parameter
source_issues.evidence: Azure OpenAI new API version returns 400 BadRequestError because Goose sends api-version query parameter which is no longer allowed. Links to specific source lines in providers/azure.rs.

signals.topic: MCP extension processes leak memory and persist as orphans after Goose session ends
signals.summary: MCP extension processes (Slack, Google Drive, Snowflake, etc.) spawned during Goose sessions are not cleaned up on session end, causing severe memory leak with up to 187 orphaned Python processes consuming ~2.9GB RAM.
aliases: MCP processes not cleaned up memory leak
signals.review_reason: MCP processes leak after every unclean session exit, accumulating up to ~2.9GB RAM and 187 processes. This is a real cost/resource impact that worsens over time. While closed after a PR, it represents a confirmed systemic issue affecting all MCP users.

source_issues.title: MCP extension processes are not cleaned up when Goose sessions end, causing memory leak
source_issues.evidence: 187 orphaned Python MCP processes consuming ~2.9GB RAM after unclean session shutdown. Each new session spawns ~20 more processes. 356 stale MCP processes totaling ~3.9GB. PR #3638 cleaned shell subprocesses but not MCP servers. Issue was closed after PR merge.

signals.topic: StagehandLogger 缺少 warning 方法导致 init 在只读文件系统上崩溃
signals.summary: 当 downloads_path 指向只读分区时，stagehand.init() 调用 logger.warning() 报错 AttributeError: 'StagehandLogger' object has no attribute 'warning'，导致初始化流程直接崩溃阻断。
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 构成真实用户痛点：stagehand.init() 流程在遇到只读文件系统时并未优雅降级，而是因 StagehandLogger 缺少 warning 方法导致 AttributeError 崩溃，初始化流程被阻断，用户完全无法使用 stagehand。属于主流程阻断 + 崩溃问题，虽 count=1 但有明确的堆栈证据和复现步骤，置信度高。

source_issues.title: Logger error: 'StagehandLogger' object has no attribute 'warning'
source_issues.evidence: 在 downloads_path 挂载为只读分区时调用 stagehand.init()，触发 OSError 后进入异常处理，logger.warning() 抛出 AttributeError 导致进程崩溃，stagehand 完全无法初始化。

signals.topic: Sandbox执行环境多场景失败：Session not found / 404 / 工具无法执行 / Server disconnected
signals.summary: Sandbox 执行环境在多种场景下失败：(1) Session not found (404)；(2) bash/ls/read_file 工具完全无法执行；(3) 间歇性 Server disconnected；(4) Provisioner 返回 500。均为 sandbox 基础设施故障，导致 Agent 无法使用工具，主流程彻底阻断。
aliases: Sandbox tool execution failures: session not found, tool not working, server disconnected, provisioner 500
signals.review_reason: Sandbox 是 DeerFlow Agent 执行工具的核心基础设施，4条独立 issue 从不同角度（404 session / 工具全不可用 / 间歇断连 / provisioner 500）描述了 sandbox 执行失败，导致 Agent 无法运行任何工具，主流程完全阻断。count=4 且所有场景均指向 sandbox 基础设施，满足 P0 高频+阻断条件。

source_issues.title: Failed to execute command in sandbox: status_code: 404, body: {'success': False, 'message': 'Session not found'}
source_issues.evidence: 用户执行 make docker-start 后，sandbox API 返回 404 Session not found，Agent 无法执行任何命令。

source_issues.title: 系统里无法执行bash
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确报告 bash、ls、read_file 工具均无法执行，3条评论讨论根因。

source_issues.title: [runtime] Sandbox container 'Server disconnected without sending a response' due to unnecessary services consuming resources
source_issues.evidence: sandbox 容器健康检查通过太早（supervisord 在 gem-server 初始化完成前就宣布 running），导致8次连续 Server disconnected 错误。

source_issues.title: provisioner 服务 (http://provisioner:8002/api/sandboxes) 持续返回 500 Internal Server Error
source_issues.evidence: 在 Windows WSL + Docker 环境下，provisioner 服务持续返回 500 错误，2条评论讨论此问题。

signals.topic: Chat input box blocks user interaction in New Chat view
signals.summary: 用户在新建聊天页面无法在输入框中输入任何内容，导致无法发起任何对话，主流程完全阻断。
aliases: Cannot type in New Chat input field
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：用户无法在新建聊天页面输入任何文字，无法发起任何对话。这是核心交互入口的硬性失败，属于P0级别。用户明确描述了'cannot type'，虽然只有1条issue，但影响的是所有新用户首次使用体验。

source_issues.title: typing New chat
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确描述 'I cant type in New Chat'，且有1条评论确认此问题，主流程输入完全阻断。

signals.topic: Docker deployment fails: nginx crashes with invalid 'resolve' parameter in config
signals.summary: 执行 make docker-start 后 nginx 持续崩溃重启，错误为 'invalid parameter "resolve" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf'，导致 Docker 部署模式无法正常启动，用户无法使用 DeerFlow。
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断且影响主部署路径：make docker-start 是官方推荐部署方式，nginx 启动失败意味着整个服务不可用。虽然只有1条issue，但nginx崩溃是可复现的确定性问题，影响所有通过 Docker 方式部署的用户，且有明确的错误日志和截图证据。

source_issues.title: [runtime] 执行make docker-start之后nginx一直在重启
source_issues.evidence: nginx.conf 第25行包含非法的 'resolve' 参数导致 [emerg] invalid parameter 错误，nginx 无法启动，4条评论确认此问题，是 make docker-start 主部署命令的阻断性故障。

signals.topic: LocalSandbox模式下工具间路径处理逻辑不一致，导致文件读写与执行流程断裂
signals.summary: read_file/write_file/ls 工具与 bash 工具对虚拟路径和系统路径的处理方式不同，导致 Agent 无法完成「写文件后运行」的常见工作流（写出的脚本内含虚拟路径导致执行失败），同时 ls 输出的路径格式不一致造成 Agent 困惑。
aliases: LocalSandbox path translation inconsistency between tools
Virtual path vs system path mismatch breaks write-then-execute workflow
signals.review_reason: 影响典型的代码编写-执行工作流，是 LocalSandbox 模式下的结构性设计缺陷，而非偶发问题。Agent 无法可靠完成「写文件→运行」这类最常见的多步任务，体验显著下降。虽然只来自1条 issue，但根因清晰且覆盖了 read_file/write_file/ls/bash 所有工具的交互，修复难度高、影响面广。

source_issues.title: LocalSandbox模式下各工具处理路径的逻辑不一致导致找不到文件和路径
source_issues.evidence: 用户通过截图详细展示了两种工具对路径处理的不一致：bash 工具会将命令行参数和输出中的虚拟路径互相转换，而 read_file/write_file 不做内容转换。导致 Agent 先用 write_file 写入含虚拟路径的 Python 脚本，再通过 bash 执行时路径不存在。这是一个完整的典型工作流断裂。

signals.topic: ACP agent调用失败：mcp_servers 格式错误导致 validation error
signals.summary: ACP 协议中 NewSessionRequest 期望 mcp_servers 为 list 格式，但 DeerFlow _build_mcp_servers() 函数返回 dict 格式，导致 ACP agent（如 claude_code）调用时 validation 报错，ACP agent 工具完全不可用。
aliases: ACP agent invocation validation error: dict vs list format for mcp_servers
signals.review_reason: ACP agent 工具是 DeerFlow 调用外部 Agent（如 claude_code）的关键能力，格式错误使其完全不可用。虽然只有1条 issue，但问题根因明确（dict vs list 类型不匹配）、错误日志完整，影响意图使用 ACP 协议的用户的核心功能。

source_issues.title: [runtime] [error] ACP agent 'claude_code' invocation failed: 1 validation error for NewSessionRequest
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确报告 ACP 开启后运行报错，_build_mcp_servers() 返回 dict 但 ACP 协议期望 list，日志显示 'ACP agent invocation failed: 1 validation error for NewSessionRequest'。

signals.topic: ACT MODE (Tab) UI indicator shows Act mode but system remains in PLAN MODE, blocking file write tools
signals.summary: After switching to ACT MODE via Tab or -p parameter, the UI shows '● Act (Tab)' but environment details still show 'Current Mode: PLAN MODE'. The write_to_file tool is unavailable with error 'Tool write_to_file is not available in PLAN MODE'. The mode switch desync is self-validating — an AI assistant generating the bug report is itself stuck in PLAN MODE.
signals.review_reason: The ACT/Plan mode desync completely blocks the core file modification workflow — the primary action users need from ACT mode. The UI lies about the system state, and the bug is self-confirming (the reporting AI is itself stuck). Two separate reports confirm this is reproducible via different triggers (Tab shortcut and -p parameter).

source_issues.title: ACT MODE (Tab)工具不可用问题 / ACT MODE (Tab) Tools Unavailable Issue
source_issues.evidence: UI shows '● Act (Tab)' but environment state is PLAN MODE. write_to_file tool returns 'Tool write_to_file is not available in PLAN MODE'. The AI assistant generating the report is itself stuck in PLAN MODE, confirming the desync.

source_issues.title: [Bug] write_to_file tool becomes unresponsive after switching from Plan to Act mode via shortcut
source_issues.evidence: After using the mode-switch shortcut, write_to_file stops working and becomes unresponsive. Restart temporarily resolves but it reoccurs on next mode switch.

signals.topic: Terminal heredoc/heredoc-style commands cause output capture failure and UI freeze
signals.summary: Heredoc-style inline scripts (bash `<<`) executed via execute_command result in 'result missing' or hang. Cancel button then deadlocks the UI (greyed out, no Resume, no new messages). Manual terminal execution of the same heredoc succeeds, confirming Cline's terminal capture logic is broken for this syntax.
signals.review_reason: Heredoc command execution blocks the main coding workflow. The output capture failure causes steps to hang with no resolution, and Cancel then deadlocks the chat UI, making the extension unusable for that conversation. Verified by manual control test showing same heredoc works in standard terminal.

source_issues.title: Heredoc execution breaks terminal output handling (`result missing`/hang), and Cancel may freeze chat UI
source_issues.evidence: Heredoc commands executed via Cline produce 'result missing' or hang indefinitely. Manual terminal execution of the same commands succeeds. Cancel button deadlocks the UI (greyed out, no Resume, cannot send new messages).

signals.topic: execute_command renders shell operators as HTML entities (&&&), causing bash syntax errors and process stall
signals.summary: When the model emits chained shell commands, && operators are rendered as HTML-escaped &&, causing 'syntax error near unexpected token' and leaving the process stuck.
aliases: HTML entity escaped in bash command
signals.review_reason: Command execution with chained shell operators fails completely due to HTML entity escaping, blocking any workflow using &&. The process then stalls with no recovery. This is a direct execution failure affecting the core use case of running shell commands.

source_issues.title: execute_command renders && literally in bash command, causing `syntax error near unexpected token`;`;' and stuck process
source_issues.evidence: Model emits execute_command with && (HTML-escaped) instead of &&. Bash fails with syntax error and process gets stuck. Multiple bash commands fail due to this rendering bug.

signals.topic: Terminal/process hangs after bash syntax error instead of returning error and completing
signals.summary: When a shell command triggers a bash parse error (e.g., unescaped quotes/parens in arguments), the terminal integration stalls indefinitely rather than returning the error with a non-zero exit code.
signals.review_reason: A bash syntax error causes the entire tool execution to hang indefinitely rather than cleanly returning an error. This blocks the workflow for any command that triggers a parse error, with no timeout or recovery mechanism visible to the user.

source_issues.title: Terminal stalls after bash syntax error when command contains escaped quotes/parentheses
source_issues.evidence: Commands with unescaped quotes/parentheses cause bash syntax errors and then the terminal/process hangs indefinitely. Tool execution does not complete normally after the error.

signals.topic: Kanban CLI fails to restore session/task state after process crash, cards lost or permanently stuck
signals.summary: When the Kanban process crashes (e.g., OOM in WSL), restarting leaves task cards in an inconsistent state. Cards end up in trash, restore operation is slow and unreliable, and tasks appear 'in progress' but do not actually advance.
aliases: kanban session state lost on restart
kanban cards in trash after crash
signals.review_reason: After process crash, Kanban loses all session/task state with unreliable recovery. Users lose visibility into what was in progress and cannot resume work, directly causing workflow disruption and lost productivity in a session-management feature.

source_issues.title: cline kanban: not restoring sessions after process crash
source_issues.evidence: WSL crash during Kanban use. After restart, cards are in trash, restore is very slow and unreliable, tasks show 'in progress' but do not progress. Significant user workflow disruption with lost state.

signals.topic: OpenAI Responses API reasoning models (o1/o3-mini) violate item sequencing requirements causing 400/500 errors when using tools
signals.summary: The OpenAI Responses API enforces strict adjacency between 'reasoning' items and their associated output items. Current code emits function_call items before text message items, breaking the required sequence and triggering 400/500 errors whenever reasoning models attempt tool calls.
aliases: OpenAI reasoning model tool call 400 Bad Request
o1/o3-mini Responses API item sequencing violation
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：使用o1/o3-mini等推理模型时工具调用完全失败，同时触发400和500错误。3条issue确认同一API适配层缺陷，count=3。

source_issues.title: [Bug] OpenAI Responses API 400 Bad Request: 'Missing reasoning item' with Reasoning Models
source_issues.evidence: 400 Bad Request: "Item was provided without its required 'reasoning' item." Root cause: toResponsesInput emits function_call before text message, violating API's reasoning/message adjacency requirement.

source_issues.title: [Bug] 500 Internal Server Error in OpenAI o1/o3-mini Reasoning API when using tools
source_issues.evidence: 500 Internal Server Error caused by sanitizeResponsesInput stripping function_call IDs without also stripping orphaned function_call_output items, creating malformed request payloads.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Tool call duplication in UI when streaming with OpenAI Responses API
source_issues.evidence: Tool call deltas lack index property, causing UI to treat each streaming chunk as a new tool execution instead of merging, resulting in "Attempted X actions" duplication bug. (Resolved via PR adding index to ToolCallDelta.)

signals.topic: IntelliJ glob/file search missing maxResults limit causing context window overflow in large repositories
signals.summary: The IntelliJ implementation does not enforce maxResults when returning glob/file search results, causing the entire file list to be returned in large repos (10k+ files), which immediately exhausts the LLM context window and blocks the @codebase and other file-search features.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：@codebase和文件搜索功能在大型仓库中完全不可用。2条独立issue均确认同一根因（IntelliJ getFileResults缺少maxResults截断），count=2。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Missing results limitation in IntelliJ getFileResults implementation causing context overflow
source_issues.evidence: Entire file list returned for **/* glob in 10k+ file repo → 400 Bad Request due to context length exceeded. Root cause: messageIde.ts fails to forward maxResults, and IntelliJ implementation lacks truncation logic.

source_issues.title: [Bug] IntelliJ file search results exceed limits and cause token overflow
source_issues.evidence: File search returns all matched files without limit, leading to context window overflow. VS Code enforces maxResults=100 but IntelliJ does not. PR fix: add take(maxResults) on returned file list.

signals.topic: Continue credits/plan system shows incorrect balance despite paid subscription — users unable to use service
signals.summary: Users with active paid subscriptions and existing credits ($54 balance reported) are shown 'insufficient credits' errors and prompted to purchase more, despite already having a paid account. This blocks all usage for affected users.
aliases: Credits not recognized despite paid account
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+成本损失：付费用户无法使用服务，计费系统未正确识别用户余额和配置。2条issue确认同一计费识别问题，count=2，影响明确。

source_issues.title: You don't have enough credits? seriously
source_issues.evidence: User shows $54 credit balance in UI but extension repeatedly prompts to purchase more credits. User unable to use service despite having paid credits.

source_issues.title: Error: Claude Sonnet 4.5 - 402
source_issues.evidence: 402 Payment Required: 'No credits remaining on Continue account' even after adding ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. User's configured key not being used, continue-proxy billing system not recognizing valid credentials.

signals.topic: Local autocomplete broken in VSCode — LM Studio streaming disconnects prematurely, zero tokens returned
signals.summary: Autocomplete with local LM Studio models fails: the server streams a response but the Continue extension disconnects prematurely, returning zero generated tokens. The extension has been non-functional for autocomplete use cases, with a known regression spanning months.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：本地模型自动补全功能完全失效，用户长期受影响且有历史回归记录。虽然count=1，但影响的是核心功能（autocomplete），且用户明确引用了历史issue说明长期存在的问题。

source_issues.title: Local Autocomplete Broken!
source_issues.evidence: LM Studio server log shows 'Client disconnected. Stopping generation' immediately after first token. Extension returns Result: Success with Prompt Tokens: 0, Generated Tokens: 0. User reports extension has been broken for nearly a year (references issue #5079).

signals.topic: VSCode extension causes high CPU load and IDE crash when editing files
signals.summary: The Continue VSCode extension causes high CPU load and can crash the entire IDE when performing file edit operations. The crash occurs immediately when trying to edit files, making the extension unusable.
aliases: VSCode high cpu load continue extension
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断且体验严重下降：VSCode IDE在编辑文件时直接崩溃，扩展完全不可用。虽然count=1，但崩溃行为属于严重阻断性问题，且无任何workaround。

source_issues.title: IDE Crashes
source_issues.evidence: Entire IDE crashes immediately when trying to edit a file using Continue. Occurs in both stock VSCode and alternative IDEs. No workaround available.

signals.topic: Async workflow performs synchronous blocking LLM calls in _export_output/converter module, blocking the event loop
signals.summary: When a CrewAI workflow is started via `akickoff()` (async path), the `_export_output` method and converter module make synchronous `self.llm.call()` invocations. These block the event loop, defeating the purpose of async workflows and breaking async-first usage patterns. The issue is confirmed at specific code locations in task.py and converter.py with concrete call sites.
aliases: synchronous LLM call in async task export
event loop blocking in async workflow
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with clear root cause and specific code locations. Blocks the primary async kickoff flow by synchronously blocking the event loop. Users running async workflows via `akickoff()` experience main-flow blocking when task output requires format conversion.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Do not invoke synchronous `call()` on LLM from asynchronous workflow in `_export_output` / converter
source_issues.evidence: Async workflow via `akickoff()` makes synchronous `self.llm.call()` in converter module. Blocks the event loop. Call sites confirmed in task.py lines 605 and 1258. Directly breaks async-first workflows.

signals.topic: InternalInstructor silently discards base_url when using OpenAI-compatible endpoints, routing to wrong API
signals.summary: When configuring an LLM with a custom `base_url` (e.g., self-hosted vLLM, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), InternalInstructor's `_create_instructor_client()` extracts only the model name and provider string, then calls `instructor.from_provider()` which creates a fresh client defaulting to api.openai.com. The base_url is never forwarded. Users silently get wrong API responses, hallucinations, or unexpected billing on OpenAI's infrastructure instead of their intended provider.
aliases: base_url not forwarded to instructor client
wrong API endpoint called due to base_url drop
OpenAI-compatible provider silently routed to OpenAI
signals.review_reason: Confirmed silent failure bug. Users configuring self-hosted vLLM, Ollama, or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints have their `base_url` silently discarded and get routed to api.openai.com. Results in wrong model responses, hallucinations, and unexpected OpenAI API billing instead of the intended provider.

source_issues.title: [BUG] InternalInstructor discards base_url when creating instructor client — breaks OpenAI-compatible endpoints
source_issues.evidence: Root cause in `internal_instructor.py`: `_create_instructor_client()` calls `instructor.from_provider(f'{provider}/{model_string}')` without forwarding `base_url`. The `_get_llm_extra_kwargs()` method that does forward `base_url` is guarded behind `is_litellm=True`. Users of vLLM, Ollama, and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints silently hit api.openai.com instead.

signals.topic: KeyError crash in _handle_non_streaming_response when 'messages' key is missing from params dict
signals.summary: In `crewai/llm.py`, both `_handle_non_streaming_response()` (line 1220) and `_ahandle_non_streaming_response()` (line 1364) access `params['messages']` directly in `_handle_emit_call_events`, even though `params.get('messages', [])` was already used to extract and validate messages earlier in the same method. When `messages` key is absent from `params`, the code raises a confusing `KeyError` instead of the more informative `ValueError` already raised earlier in the validation path. This crashes the LLM response handling path.
aliases: KeyError in LLM response handler when messages missing
confusing error instead of helpful ValueError in response handling
signals.review_reason: Confirmed crash bug in the core LLM response handling path. When `messages` key is absent from params dict (especially with `response_model` set), the code crashes with a confusing KeyError instead of the existing helpful ValueError. Breaks the LLM response processing flow.

source_issues.title: [BUG] KeyError when params missing 'messages' key in _handle_non_streaming_response
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed crash bug at line 1220/1364 of llm.py. Code validates messages via `params.get('messages', [])` then immediately accesses `params['messages']` in `_handle_emit_call_events`. Raises confusing KeyError instead of the existing ValueError. Reproducible when `response_model` is set and messages key is absent.

signals.topic: MCPToolResolver silently returns empty tool list without warning, causing UnboundLocalError downstream
signals.summary: `MCPToolResolver._resolve_native()` silently returns an empty tool list when the MCP server returns no tools or when `tool_filter` removes all tools. No warning is logged, making it extremely difficult for users to debug why their MCP server (Stdio/HTTP/SSE) is not providing tools. The empty `tools_list` can trigger an `UnboundLocalError` at `tool_resolver.py` line 412. In contrast, `_resolve_external()` (for HTTPS MCP URLs) correctly logs a warning.
aliases: MCP tools silently empty with no warning
no debug logging when MCP server returns zero tools
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug causing silent failure and a downstream UnboundLocalError crash. MCP tool resolution silently returns empty results with no logging, making it near-impossible for users to debug why their MCP server configuration yields no tools. Breaks MCP integration for any user whose server returns zero tools or whose filter removes all results.

source_issues.title: [BUG] MCPToolResolver does not log warning when native MCP config returns no tools
source_issues.evidence: Bug in `crewai/mcp/tool_resolver.py` `_resolve_native()` method. Silently returns empty `tools_list` without logging, unlike `_resolve_external()` which logs 'No tools discovered from MCP server'. Empty list causes UnboundLocalError at line 412. Users of Stdio/HTTP/SSE MCP servers get cryptic runtime errors with no clue about root cause.
