signals.topic: Session resume fails with 'Invalid session identifier' — session not persisted after close
signals.summary: Multiple users cannot resume sessions after quitting; the session JSON file is either not written or silently lost, making the --resume feature completely unreliable.
signals.review_reason: Session resume is a core user workflow — losing a 1h15m session with 54 tool calls due to silent persistence failure is high-severity data loss. Two independent reports confirm a systemic issue with session file writes not being completed. The 'possible-duplicate' label on #24535 suggests the underlying bug has recurred across versions without a proper fix.

source_issues.title: Failed to resume previous conversations — "Invalid session identifier" error
source_issues.evidence: User runs gemini --resume with the exact session ID provided by CLI at end of session; CLI responds 'Invalid session identifier'. Affects multiple versions (0.36.0 and all previous). Session file is missing despite logs showing the session existed.

source_issues.title: Unable to resume session after just closing it and copying very session ID; session gone (probably never recorded) ! (Multiple times)
source_issues.evidence: User loses session after 1h15m work session (54 tool calls, 70% success rate). Logs confirm session activity but session JSON file is never written. Reproduced multiple times by same user in one day. /resume list also fails to show the session.

signals.topic: Replace tool corrupts/blanks entire file on Windows when sandbox is enabled
signals.summary: When using the file Replace tool on Windows with sandbox, the diff preview looks correct but upon approval the entire file gets wiped, causing permanent data loss.
aliases: file content lost after replace approval
signals.review_reason: File content destruction is a critical data-loss issue. The replace tool is central to the CLI's core value proposition. The diff preview shows correct changes but the result is a blank file — users cannot trust the preview. Already tagged P0 by project maintainers.

source_issues.title: Replace tool broken in windows with sandbox
source_issues.evidence: User verified diff looks correct in VSCode diff view before approval. After approval CLI churns for a long time then the file is completely blanked. Already labeled P0 by maintainers. 5 comments indicate active investigation and the issue is reproducible.

signals.topic: CLI hangs indefinitely on 'Thinking' state — unresponsive despite AI Pro subscription
signals.summary: CLI remains stuck in 'Thinking...' state for simple prompts, never returning a response, even with a paid Google One AI Pro subscription.
signals.review_reason: CLI becomes completely unusable — a main-flow failure. The user has a paid subscription and cannot use the product at all. The Thinking state hangs indefinitely on even trivial prompts, preventing any productive use of the tool.

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI v0.36.0 hangs on "Thinking" indefinitely (>5m) despite AI Pro subscription
source_issues.evidence: Simple 'Hellow' prompt hangs for over 2 seconds minimum and never returns a response. User has an active Google One AI Pro subscription. CLI is completely unusable — no response is ever produced for any prompt.

signals.topic: MCP/JIRA integration causes infinite loop — consumes all available tokens with no output
signals.summary: Connecting to a JIRA MCP server triggers an infinite loop that rapidly exhausts the user's entire token quota without producing any useful result.
aliases: JIRA MCP infinite loop token drain
signals.review_reason: Uncontrolled infinite loop causing total token quota exhaustion is direct financial harm to the user. It also renders the entire MCP integration feature unusable. This meets the threshold of 'obvious cost loss' with zero user benefit.

source_issues.title: tried to connect to jira mcp and it just run in an infinite loop consuming ALL my tokens
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states 'consuming ALL my tokens' from a JIRA MCP integration. This is an uncontrolled token drain with direct monetary cost to the user and zero productive output.

signals.topic: Google One AI Ultra accounts receive 403 PERMISSION_DENIED — CLI unusable despite recognized subscription
signals.summary: AI Ultra subscribers can authenticate successfully and see their tier recognized in /about, but every API request fails with 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, making the CLI entirely unusable for this tier.
signals.review_reason: AI Ultra is the highest-paid tier, and those users cannot use the product at all due to an auth routing bug. This is a key functional blocker for premium users. Marked P1 instead of P0 because count=1, but the impact is severe — a paying customer with the top-tier subscription is completely blocked.

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI 0.36.0 returns 403 PERMISSION_DENIED for Google One AI Ultra account

signals.topic: Agent memory cannot be persisted across sessions — save/load agent memory is missing
signals.summary: MultiStepAgent does not support saving and loading its conversation memory (history/messages). Users who need to resume agent sessions cannot persist state, and custom step_callbacks/final_answer_checks are also lost after serialization round-trip via save() and from_folder().
aliases: save and restore agent conversation history
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 共同指向同一根因：agent 内存/状态无法在会话间持久化。#1216 明确指出用户有跨会话恢复 agent 状态的需求但完全找不到方案；#2142 进一步揭示即使用户自行实现了 save/from_folder 流程，自定义 callbacks 也会丢失。这不是边缘改进，而是关键持久化能力的缺失，直接影响需要长时任务或状态恢复的生产场景。

source_issues.title: Save/Load agent memory
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly searched for a way to save agent memory after session ends and reload it later but found no available method. Issue has 6 comments indicating sustained user interest.

source_issues.title: feat: support serialization for step_callbacks and final_answer_checks in MultiStepAgent
source_issues.evidence: Custom step_callbacks and final_answer_checks are explicitly ignored in to_dict() during agent serialization. When agent is saved via save() and reloaded via from_folder(), custom callbacks are lost. Users must manually re-register callbacks after every load.

signals.topic: ToolSerializer.dumps f-string escape bug produces literal '{e}' instead of actual exception message
signals.summary: When pickle serialization fails in ToolSerializer.dumps, users see the uninformative literal string 'Cannot serialize object: {e}' instead of the actual exception details, making serialization failures extremely difficult to debug.
aliases: f-string double braces bug in serialization error messages
signals.review_reason: 用户调试序列化失败时，错误信息完全不可用——只显示字面量 '{e}' 而非真实异常内容，直接阻断调试流程。这不是功能缺失，而是现有功能产生了误导性输出，迫使用户自行追踪源码才能理解真实错误原因，造成明确的体验下降和主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: BUG: f-string escape error in ToolSerializer.dumps causes uninformative error message
source_issues.evidence: Line 429 in serialization.py uses double braces {{e}} which produces literal '{e}' instead of interpolating the exception variable. Users debugging serialization failures see 'Cannot serialize object: {e}' with no actual error context.

signals.topic: GitHub Actions workflow token permissions causing 403 error during artifact deletion in Copilot code review cleanup job
signals.summary: The Copilot code review cleanup job in GitHub Actions repeatedly fails with HTTP 403 (Resource not accessible by integration) when attempting to delete artifacts. This blocks the automated CI workflow from completing cleanly, requiring manual intervention or leaving orphaned artifacts.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user-facing CI/CD workflow blockage. The Copilot code review cleanup job consistently fails with a 403 error, preventing the automated workflow from completing. This constitutes a workflow-level runtime failure that affects the project's development process. While count=1 precludes a P0 rating, the failure is clearly reproducible (specific run ID cited) with a known root cause (workflow token permissions). The artifact cleanup step fails fast rather than degrading gracefully, leaving orphaned artifacts and requiring manual intervention. This meets the threshold for a real user pain point.

source_issues.title: Copilot code review cleanup job fails deleting artifacts with 403
source_issues.evidence: Workflow run 23775280758 fails in the 'Cleanup artifacts' step with exit code 1 and error: 'gh: Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)'. The job blocks the Copilot code review workflow from completing. Root cause identified as workflow token permissions / integration scope mismatch during artifact deletion.

These collectively degrade the user experience of the approval/input workflow.
aliases: Ask user tool overflow scroll multiline
signals.review_reason: Multiple UI interaction issues in the Ask user component that degrade the user approval/input workflow. Count=5 confirmed from distinct issues, all from the same maintainer. Non-blocking but collectively represent a pattern of UX neglect in a key user-facing interaction surface.

signals.topic: MCP servers appear duplicated in approval prompt when both .mcp.json and .deepagents/.mcp.json config files exist
signals.summary: When a project contains both root .mcp.json and .deepagents/.mcp.json (e.g., when using rulesync), deepagents reads both files without deduplication, causing shared MCP servers to appear twice in the startup approval prompt. Users must approve the same server twice, causing confusion.
aliases: MCP server duplication in approval prompt
MCP servers appear twice startup approval
signals.review_reason: Confusing user experience: same server appears twice requiring duplicate approvals. Directly impacts any user with MCP servers in both config file locations, which is a common pattern for rulesync users. Count=2 confirmed via two distinct issue reports.

source_issues.title: MCP servers duplicated in approval prompt when both `.mcp.json` and `.deepagents/.mcp.json` exist

signals.topic: Windows CLI startup crashes with UnicodeDecodeError due to missing UTF-8 encoding in file operations
signals.summary: On Windows, deepagents CLI fails to start with a UnicodeDecodeError ('gbk' codec cannot decode UTF-8 bytes) because Python file operations default to GBK encoding instead of UTF-8 when no encoding is specified. This completely blocks all Windows users from using the CLI.
signals.review_reason: Windows users cannot launch the CLI at all — full startup blockage with a clear crash trace. Every Windows user is affected. Count=1 but P0 due to complete CLI unavailability for entire Windows user base.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Windows: UnicodeDecodeError when starting server due to GBK default encoding
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows UnicodeDecodeError at server startup, blocking CLI from launching entirely on Windows. Root cause identified as missing encoding='utf-8' in open() calls. Reproducible on Windows 10/11 with Python 3.11+.

signals.topic: SubAgentMiddleware regression: runtime.context is None in subagent tool invocations after PR #1041 refactor
signals.summary: PR #1041 dropped the runtime.config pass-through from _build_task_tool(), reversing the fix from PR #602. Subagents invoked via the task tool receive runtime.context=None, breaking context-dependent tool functionality in multi-agent workflows.
signals.review_reason: Breaks a key multi-agent workflow pattern. All users who rely on subagent context passing are blocked from using that functionality. Clear regression with known fix.

source_issues.title: SubAgentMiddleware regression — runtime config not passed to subagent invocations (PR #602 fix lost in #1041 refactor)
source_issues.evidence: Regression from a prior fix (PR #602). Subagent tools receive runtime.context=None instead of the intended context. Clear code reproduction provided. One-line fix identified (pass runtime.config to subagent.invoke/ainvoke). Breaks any multi-agent workflow relying on context passing.

signals.topic: read_file tool on PDF/binary documents crashes with Bedrock Converse due to missing document.name field
signals.summary: FilesystemMiddleware returns a file content block without a 'name' key when reading PDFs. Bedrock Converse API requires the 'name' field for document-type content blocks, causing ParamValidationError and preventing agents from reading PDF files when using AWS Bedrock.
aliases: PDF file reading fails Bedrock Converse
signals.review_reason: Agents using AWS Bedrock cannot read PDF or other document files at all — causes a ParamValidationError crash. Clear API incompatibility with a documented fix.

source_issues.title: `read_file` on PDF/binary files fails with Bedrock Converse (Missing required parameter: `document.name`)
source_issues.evidence: Full ParamValidationError traceback provided. Bug is reproducible: use ChatBedrockConverse + read_file on any PDF. Root cause: FilesystemMiddleware returns type:file block without name field, but Bedrock Converse API requires name for document blocks. Fix identified: add name field using Path(file_path).stem.

signals.topic: filter_messages docstring uses wrong parameter names causing TypeError for users copying examples
signals.summary: The docstring example in filter_messages passes wrong kwargs (incl_names, incl_types, excl_ids) that do not match the actual function signature (include_names, include_types, exclude_ids). Anyone copying the example directly from the docs hits an immediate TypeError. Two separate issues filed on the same day by the same author confirm this is a live user-impacting bug.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed P1: docstring is user-facing and copying examples is the primary onboarding path. TypeError immediately on first use is a clear experience-breaking issue. Count=2 because both 36463 (open) and 36461 (closed as dup) are independent GitHub issues — downgraded to P1 because count=2 is low and both are in the same repo.

source_issues.title: bug(core): filter_messages docstring example uses wrong parameter names

source_issues.title: bug(core): filter_messages docstring example uses wrong parameter names
source_issues.evidence: Closed as duplicate of 36463. Same root cause. Confirms two independent reports of same user-facing docstring bug.

signals.topic: Anthropic Thinking mode + structured output / tool use causes 400 API error and blocks agent workflow
signals.summary: When using ChatAnthropic with thinking mode enabled (thinking={'type': 'enabled', 'budget_tokens': 1024}) alongside structured output (response_format=Pydantic model) and tool calls, the agent hardcodes tool_choice to 'any', which Anthropic API rejects with 'Thinking may not be enabled when tool_choice forces tool use'. This is a hard block: users cannot use Thinking + structured output + tools simultaneously in LangChain agents.
aliases: thinking mode blocks structured output with tools
signals.review_reason: Confirmed P0: user workflow is completely blocked — they cannot use Anthropic Thinking mode at all when their agent uses structured output with tools. This is not a rare edge case; it is a fundamental architectural incompatibility. Explicit error + reproduction + root cause identified.

source_issues.title: Problems with thinking/reasoning and structured output for tools using Anthropic
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible code sample produces HTTP 400 error: 'Thinking may not be enabled when tool_choice forces tool use.' Root cause: factory.py hardcodes tool_choice='any' for structured output, incompatible with Anthropic Thinking. Agent workflow is completely blocked.

signals.topic: Agent terminates on return_direct tool even when tool call fails — breaking retry flow
signals.summary: When a tool with return_direct=True fails (raises exception), the agent immediately terminates instead of routing back to the model for retry. ToolNode correctly produces a ToolMessage with status='error', but the routing logic in factory.py ignores the error status and exits the loop.
aliases: return_direct tool failure causes silent agent exit
agent exits on tool error with return_direct=True
signals.review_reason: Confirmed P0: agent silently terminates on recoverable tool failure, losing all conversation context. This is a production-breaking workflow bug — any tool error on a return_direct tool causes total mission failure. Has reproducible test case with exact code location.

source_issues.title: bug(langchain): agent terminates on return_direct tool even when tool call fails
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible test with FakeToolCallingModel. Code in factory.py lines 1797-1805 checks only return_direct flag, not ToolMessage status='error'. Expected: agent retries on failure. Actual: agent terminates, losing context.

signals.topic: OpenRouter streaming reasoning_details fragmentation causes multi-turn BadRequestResponseError
signals.summary: During streaming mode, AIMessageChunk.__add__ list-concatenates reasoning_details in additional_kwargs, fragmenting a single entry into many. When the conversation history is serialized back for multi-turn requests, the API rejects the malformed fragmented payload with BadRequestResponseError. This makes multi-turn streaming conversations completely unusable.
aliases: reasoning_details concat causes BadRequestResponseError in multi-turn
signals.review_reason: Confirmed P0: multi-turn streaming conversations completely break on Turn 2 with explicit API error. Users relying on streaming + reasoning with OpenRouter cannot have any meaningful multi-turn session — their pipeline fails silently after the first turn.

source_issues.title: fix(openrouter): streaming reasoning_details fragmentation causes multi-turn BadRequestResponseError
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows Turn 1 streaming works but Turn 2 raises BadRequestResponseError. Root cause: AIMessageChunk.__add__ concatenates reasoning_details list instead of merging. Non-streaming invoke() is unaffected.

signals.topic: ChatOpenAI drops OpenAI-compatible provider reasoning fields from responses
signals.summary: langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI silently drops provider-returned reasoning/reasoning_content fields from OpenAI-compatible backend responses. Raw HTTP, OpenAI SDK, and AsyncOpenAI all return the field, but LangChain's invoke() and stream() omit it from AIMessage.additional_kwargs and response_metadata.
aliases: ChatOpenAI loses reasoning data from compatible backends
signals.review_reason: P2: While this is a data loss issue (reasoning content silently dropped), count=1 and only affects OpenAI-compatible backends. Not a hard block — conversation continues, just without reasoning metadata. Kept because it causes observability/data loss for users who need reasoning traces. Labeled 'feature request' but describes a regression-like silent data drop.

source_issues.title: Support for reasoning
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with OpenAI-compatible backends (Qwen3.5). Raw HTTP and OpenAI SDK both return reasoning field; LangChain ChatOpenAI drops it silently. Affects observability, debugging, and evaluation pipelines.

signals.topic: Checkpoint resume from specific checkpoint_id incorrectly replays from beginning instead of resuming
signals.summary: When using Command(resume=...) with a specific checkpoint_id config, the graph replays from the start instead of resuming from the interrupt trigger point. User's multi-step agent state is lost and re-executed. Workaround: remove checkpoint_id from config.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：interrupt/resume 是 LangGraph 的核心人机交互机制。checkpoint_id 特定恢复时错误地重放整个图，导致第一个工具结果丢失。这是核心功能的回归性错误，workaround 为移除 checkpoint_id，但用户通常需要保留 checkpoint_id 来定位恢复点，影响严重。

source_issues.title: When resume from a specific checkpoint_id, it becomes replay
source_issues.evidence: Resuming interrupt with a specific checkpoint_id causes graph to replay from start. Expected: resume from interrupt trigger point. Actual: full graph re-execution, first tool message disappears. Confirmed workaround: removing checkpoint_id from config fixes it. Downgrade to langgraph 1.0.x fixes it.

signals.topic: add_messages(format='langchain-openai') silently drops message IDs and additional_kwargs
signals.summary: When using the langchain-openai format, message IDs become None and custom additional_kwargs are silently discarded. Breaks ID-based deduplication and any custom metadata stored in kwargs.
signals.review_reason: 数据完整性损坏：每次 reducer 调用都会静默丢失 message IDs 和额外元数据。这意味着基于 ID 的去重逻辑失效、自定义元数据被永久丢弃，且无任何警告或错误提示。用户体验影响显著但非全局阻断，故评为 P1。

source_issues.title: bug: add_messages(format='langchain-openai') strips message IDs and additional_kwargs
source_issues.evidence: add_messages with format='langchain-openai' silently sets all message IDs to None and drops custom additional_kwargs to {}. Root cause: _format_messages() calls convert_to_openai_messages() without include_id=True. Impact: ID-based deduplication breaks on every reducer call; custom data (UI widgets, metadata) silently lost.

signals.topic: Command.PARENT discards parallel tool call results when multiple tools called in same turn
signals.summary: When a model calls multiple tools in parallel and tools return Command.PARENT with goto, only the last tool's result is kept. Other parallel tool results are silently dropped, causing data loss in multi-tool workflows.
aliases: multi-tool goto parent silently loses results
signals.review_reason: 并行工具调用结果静默丢失：当模型在单轮中并行调用多个工具并返回 Command.PARENT 时，仅最后一个结果被保留，其余被丢弃。这是数据丢失型 bug，在现代多工具 Agent 中会频繁出现，因为新版模型（如 gemini-3-flash）原生支持并行工具调用。

source_issues.title: Command.PARENT does not work with parallel tool calls
source_issues.evidence: With newer models calling multiple tools in one turn, each tool returning Command.PARENT causes only the last result to be kept. All prior parallel tool results are silently discarded. Reproduction shows tools_called={'a','b','c'} but only one ends up in state. Root cause: raise at langgraph/graph/state.py line 1550.

signals.topic: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch acquires redundant unused connection per call, wasting pool capacity
signals.summary: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch acquires a connection via get_connection but doesn't use it. A second connection is then acquired inside _cursor, resulting in two connections checked out for one actual I/O operation. In high-concurrency environments, this doubles connection pressure.
signals.review_reason: 连接资源浪费：abatch 每调用一次就多占用一个连接，造成连接池压力翻倍。在高并发 Postgres 生产环境中，这会直接导致连接耗尽、请求排队甚至拒绝服务。已有明确的代码层面根因，确认为用户影响。

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch acquires unused connection and double-checks out from pool
source_issues.evidence: abatch calls _ainternal.get_connection() but never uses it. _execute_batch then calls _cursor which calls get_connection again and uses that second connection. Result: two connections checked out per abatch call, only one used. Doubles connection pressure on pool under load.

signals.topic: AsyncPostgresSaver instance-level threading.Lock serializes all async DB operations, crushing throughput
signals.summary: AsyncPostgresSaver uses instance-level threading.Lock across async cursor methods, serializing all concurrent asyncio tasks within the same process. Benchmark shows throughput drops from 1295 to 200 req/s (6.5x) and median latency rises from 88ms to 2000ms.
signals.review_reason: 严重性能劣化：实测异步 Postgres checkpointer 因锁导致吞吐量下降 6.5 倍、中位延迟上升 22 倍。这在生产高并发场景（Cloud SQL + GKE 真实环境）下直接导致服务降级和资源浪费。虽然没有功能报错，但用户体验等同于不可用。

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresSaver enforces instance-level threading.Lock() during asynchronous execution
source_issues.evidence: GKE + Cloud SQL PostgreSQL load test (500 concurrent users, 60s). Baseline (raw psycopg_pool): 38044 reqs, 1295 req/s, 88ms avg. AsyncPostgresSaver: 9786 reqs, 200 req/s, 2000ms avg. Root cause: threading.Lock() across async methods serializes all concurrent asyncio tasks.

categorization client init at import time

Users who deploy openmemory in environments without OpenAI (e.g., using Ollama, Anthropic, or Gemini) cannot start the server at all. This is a startup crash that blocks the primary deployment workflow.

signals.summary: When running multi-agent SequentialBuilder/WorkflowBuilder with tool approval or handoff workflows, AzureOpenAIChatClient emits error 400: 'messages with role tool must be a response to a preceding message with tool_calls'. The tool role message is passed without its parent tool_calls message, breaking the multi-agent orchestration flow.
aliases: tool_calls/tool role message ordering broken in multi-agent workflows
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues (#5023, #5035) both affect multi-agent workflow tool-approval/handoff flows. Issue #5023 produces a hard API 400 error that completely blocks the workflow execution. Issue #5035 silently swallows approval requests, meaning users never receive the interactive prompt — both are primary flow blockers for multi-agent orchestration use cases.

source_issues.title: Python: AzureOpenAIChatClient error 400: messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceding message with 'tool_calls'

signals.topic: Workflow checkpoint/restore loses Foreach loop iteration state — loop exits immediately on resume
signals.summary: When a declarative workflow's Foreach loop contains a Human-in-the-Loop action (ExternalInputRequest), the loop terminates after the first iteration upon resume from checkpoint. The iteration index and values are lost, making long-running iterative workflows with human input unusable.
signals.review_reason: Checkpoint/restore is a core workflow resilience feature. Losing loop iteration state means users cannot resume any iterative workflow involving human input — a critical degradation of long-running workflow reliability.

source_issues.title: .NET: ForeachExecutor loses iteration state (_index, _values) after checkpoint restore — loop exits immediately on resume
source_issues.evidence: Foreach loop exits immediately after first iteration on resume; _index and _values fields are not persisted in checkpoint, causing total workflow failure for any iterative human-in-the-loop scenario

signals.topic: Workflow telemetry crashes when CodeInterpreterToolCallContent is serialized with EnableSensitiveData=true
signals.summary: In .NET, when a workflow has EnableSensitiveData=true for OpenTelemetry, the WorkflowTelemetryContext crashes when attempting to serialize messages containing CodeInterpreterToolCallContent during inter-executor messaging. This causes the entire workflow to crash.
signals.review_reason: Workflow telemetry is a core observability feature. A crash triggered by a valid combination of codeInterpreter + EnableSensitiveData=true means users cannot use observability tooling for any workflow using code interpreter — a direct functional block.

source_issues.title: .NET: Workflow telemetry crashes on CodeInterpreterToolCallContent when Workflow EnableSensitiveData = true
source_issues.evidence: Workflow crashes at WorkflowTelemetryContext serialization step when hosted agent uses codeInterpreter tool with EnableSensitiveData=true; crash is triggered by unhandled serialization of CodeInterpreterToolCallContent

signals.topic: Workflow fails end-to-end with Anthropic models due to assistant message prefill restriction
signals.summary: When two agents backed by Anthropic AnthropicClient are connected via WorkflowBuilder, the first agent's output (assistant-role messages) is passed directly as context to the second agent. Anthropic's API rejects this because it requires conversations to end with a user message. Every multi-agent workflow using Anthropic models fails on the second agent invocation.
aliases: Anthropic assistant message prefill not supported
signals.review_reason: Multi-agent workflows are a primary use case for the agent framework. Complete failure of all Anthropic-based multi-agent workflows is a significant functional gap that blocks users from using Anthropic models in production orchestration scenarios.

source_issues.title: Python: Workflow fails with Anthropic models — assistant message prefill not supported
source_issues.evidence: Anthropic API rejects workflow output because it requires conversations to end with a user message; every multi-agent workflow using Anthropic models fails on the second agent invocation

signals.topic: OpenAIEmbeddingClient fails with /openai/v1 endpoint while OpenAIChatClient succeeds

This inconsistency means Azure OpenAI embedding features are unavailable for users who have standardized on /openai/v1.
signals.review_reason: A specific client method fails with a documented 404 error. While it blocks embedding functionality for a specific endpoint pattern, it affects a narrower use case (embedding-only users) and only one client. P1 level impact but lower than multi-agent workflow blocks.

source_issues.title: Python: OpenAIEmbeddingClient does not work with /openai/v1 endpoint

signals.topic: Playwright v1.59.0 introduces multiple regressions breaking existing workflows (Codegen/UI Inspector, locator APIs, WebKit shadow DOM, test timeouts)

Downgrading to 1.58.2 resolves most issues, confirming v1.59.0 regressions.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency, multi-symptom regression in v1.59.0 causing: (1) Codegen/UI Inspector broken on Windows (blocking core feature); (2) WebKit shadow DOM fill broken (functional failure); (3) Test suite timeouts (CI blocking). All confirmed resolved by downgrading to 1.58.2.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: Codegen and UI mode doesn't open on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Codegen and UI mode Inspector window does not appear on Windows with v1.59.0. Downgrading to 1.58.2 fixes it. Affects both codegen CLI and UI mode.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: WebKit locator.fill() doesn't work for contenteditable inside shadow DOM
source_issues.evidence: In v1.59.0, WebKit's locator.fill() silently fails (empty string) for contenteditable elements inside shadow DOM. Works correctly in v1.58.2. Discovered via Vitest browser mode test suites.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: Specific tests are failing locally on Playwright version 1.59.0
source_issues.evidence: 6 tests in a real project fail on v1.59.0 with 30s timeout in beforeEach hooks waiting for locator('.Command'). Downgrading to 1.58.2 resolves. Regression compared to previous version.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: getByLabel failed in locator
source_issues.evidence: getByLabel('Password') scoped to a specific locator fails with timeout when there are duplicate labels in the document. The scoped locator should find the label within its scope but fails instead.

signals.topic: MCP server `backendPromise` not cleared on disconnect causes stale backend and 'Not connected' errors
signals.summary: When MCP server's `onClose` handler fires, it disposes the backend but does NOT clear `backendPromise`. Subsequent tool calls await the stale promise and receive a disposed backend, resulting in 'Not connected' errors with no automatic recovery. Users must restart the MCP server to recover.
aliases: MCP server stale backend after disconnect
signals.review_reason: User-facing functional failure: MCP tool calls throw 'Not connected' errors and cannot recover automatically after any disconnect event. This is a session state bug that blocks long-running MCP workflows entirely.

source_issues.title: [MCP] backendPromise not cleared in onClose causes stale backend after disconnect
source_issues.evidence: Users experience random 'Not connected' errors during long MCP sessions. Connection works initially but fails after any disconnect event, with no automatic recovery. Fix proposed with 6+ hours local testing.

signals.topic: clock.resume() causes NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED in Firefox on Linux (race condition in real-time sync loop)
signals.summary: Firefox on Linux: after clock.install() + clock.resume(), a race condition in the clock's real-time sync loop causes Firefox's setInterval to throw NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED during UI interactions (DOM re-renders), making pages blank. Reproduces reliably in Docker CI. Affects only Firefox on Linux, not macOS or other browsers.
aliases: Firefox clock API race condition Linux
signals.review_reason: User-facing functional failure in CI: clock.resume() causes pages to go blank on Linux Firefox during UI interactions. This breaks test scenarios using the clock API in Firefox CI environments.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: clock.resume() causes NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED in Firefox on Linux
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces reliably in Linux Firefox in Docker CI. During UI interactions triggering DOM re-renders (~3s after clock.resume()), NS_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED is thrown and page becomes blank. Timing trace shows exact failure point.

signals.topic: Docker image tag version mismatch: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.58.0-noble installs and runs v1.59.0, causing client-server version mismatch in CI
signals.summary: The Docker image tagged as v1.58.0 actually installs and runs Playwright v1.59.0 (via npx playwright install), causing a client-server version mismatch that blocks CI pipelines. The image name/tag no longer reflects the actual Playwright version inside, making it impossible to pin a specific version in CI.
aliases: Docker image version mismatch v1.58.0 vs v1.59.0
signals.review_reason: User-facing CI/CD breakage: Docker image tags no longer reflect the actual Playwright version, causing version mismatch errors that block CI pipelines. Users cannot reliably pin a specific Playwright version in containers.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Docker image mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.58.0-noble runs 1.59.0
source_issues.evidence: CI pipeline running yesterday succeeded; same pipeline without changes failed this morning with version mismatch error: server v1.59 vs client v1.58. Confirmed via podman run that the v1.58.0 tag image installs v1.59.0 via npx.

signals.topic: connectOverCDP() times out on Chrome M144+ remote debugging endpoints (chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging)
signals.summary: Chrome M144+ introduced a new remote debugging mechanism via chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging that exposes a different CDP endpoint format. Playwright's connectOverCDP() successfully establishes the WebSocket connection but times out waiting for expected protocol messages, making it impossible to connect to browsers using the new M144+ debugging UI.
aliases: Chrome M144 remote debugging WS endpoint timeout
signals.review_reason: Functional blocker: connectOverCDP() completely fails (30s timeout) for Chrome M144+ remote debugging, which is a new default Chrome feature. Affects AI agent workflows, on-demand browser inspection, and user debugging scenarios.

source_issues.title: [Feature]: Support Chrome M144+ Remote Debugging via chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging
source_issues.evidence: Connection times out after 30000ms. WS connects successfully but Playwright never receives expected protocol messages. Affects key use cases: debugging user's browser without restart, on-demand inspection, MCP/AI agent browser automation.

signals.topic: Python: AgentGroupChat fails when Azure Monitor telemetry is enabled due to unsupported dict response_format
signals.summary: Enabling Azure Monitor (OpenTelemetry instrumentation) causes all AgentGroupChat executions to fail with 'ValueError: Unknown response format <class dict>' because the Azure AI telemetry instrumentor does not support dict-typed response_format during agent invocation, preventing multi-agent flows from completing.
signals.review_reason: Telemetry instrumentation breaks the core multi-agent execution path. Users cannot use Azure Monitor alongside AgentGroupChat. This is a main-flow blocking issue for production monitoring scenarios. Single issue but high impact (telemetry integration is a standard production requirement).

source_issues.title: [Python] AgentGroupChat fails with 'Unknown response format <class 'dict'>' when Azure Monitor is enabled
source_issues.evidence: All agent executions fail with ValueError; automatic retries also fail; multi-agent flow is completely blocked; Azure AI telemetry instrumentor intercepts calls and does not support dict type response_format

signals.topic: .NET Gemini connector emits duplicate token usage metrics during streaming causing inflated cost tracking
signals.summary: The .NET Gemini connector emits OpenTelemetry token usage counters for every streaming chunk instead of once at the end, causing production systems to report inflated token counts and costs (e.g. $0.40 logged vs $0.02 actual).
aliases: Inflated token usage telemetry from Gemini streaming
signals.review_reason: Directly causes measurable financial cost in production via inflated telemetry billing. Metrics are systematically wrong for every Gemini streaming call. Confirmed root cause with known fix pattern from related Python bug. High impact per occurrence.

source_issues.title: .NET: Gemini connector emits duplicate token usage metrics during streaming (similar to #12977 for Python/OpenAI)
source_issues.evidence: Metrics emitted per streaming chunk (30 chunks = 30 metric events); production systems show 20x cost inflation ($0.40 vs $0.02 actual); root cause confirmed in ProcessChatResponseStreamAsync calling LogUsage() for every chunk; same pattern was a confirmed bug in Python/OpenAI (#12977)

signals.summary: When converting MCP server tools to Semantic Kernel functions, tool names containing dashes (e.g. 'create-pages') throw System.ArgumentException because plugin names only allow ASCII letters, digits, and underscores, blocking MCP integration.
aliases: MCP server tools with special characters blocked
signals.review_reason: Core MCP integration is blocked when MCP servers use standard naming conventions (dashes in tool names). This prevents users from connecting to real-world MCP servers. No workaround exists, making MCP support incomplete.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Converting MCP Tools to Kernel Function Throws System.ArgumentException
source_issues.evidence: MCP server tool names using dashes (e.g. 'create-pages') cause ArgumentException 'A plugin name can contain only ASCII letters, digits, and underscores'; blocks integration with MCP servers that use dashes in tool names; no workaround provided

source_issues.title: Python: AsyncConnectionPool Connection Timeout with Semantic Kernel PostgresSettings
source_issues.evidence: Async connection pool consistently times out after 30s; sync psycopg2 works perfectly; all tested connection string formats fail; PostgreSQL server confirmed accessible; async RAG pipelines are completely blocked

The plan detection showing '(Free)' for paid users is an unambiguous data error. source_issues.title: Codex 5-hr time runs out extremely quickly
source_issues.evidence: 5-hour usage limit exceeded in 2-3 hours after update to gpt-5.4. Previously worked fine on gpt-5.3-codex. User reports significant work disruption and others have reported the same issue.

signals.topic: CLI tool execution fails with exit code -1 and empty output, blocking core coding workflow
signals.summary: Shell/tool commands (pwd, ls, git status, sed) fail with exit code -1 and no stdout/stderr across all sessions. The agent cannot inspect workspace, verify git state, read files, or perform coding tasks — making the CLI essentially unusable for repo work. Related: image upload tool calls return 400 API errors about invalid base64 bytes, also blocking the tool-use path.
signals.review_reason: Core CLI workflow is blocked — tool execution failure renders the agent unable to perform any coding task. Exit code -1 with no output is an unambiguous, reproducible failure. Image upload errors also block a key use case. Both have clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: CLI shell/tool execution fails across sessions with exit code -1 and empty output
source_issues.evidence: Basic local shell execution broken across all coding sessions; trivial commands like `pwd`, `ls`, `git status`, `sed` fail with exit code -1 and no meaningful stdout/stderr. Failures persist across retries, across unrelated commands, and across separate sessions. Makes the coding environment mostly useless for repo work.

source_issues.title: Expected a base64-encoded data URL with an image MIME type
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 error 'Expected a base64-encoded data URL with an image MIME type, but got empty base64-encoded bytes' even for regular screenshots. Error persists after exiting and restarting Codex. Tool call path for image inputs is completely broken.

signals.topic: Resumed threads retain stale model-visible skill list after new skills are added, breaking implicit skill triggering
signals.summary: After adding new skills to a Codex session, resuming an old thread with `codex resume <thread-id>` does not update the model's visible skill inventory. The UI skill list and explicit `$skill-name` invocation work correctly, but the model-context skill section remains stale, causing implicit skill triggering to miss new skills. This is a regression in the skill hot-reload feature.
aliases: skill hot reload broken for resumed threads
implicit skill triggering fails on resume
signals.review_reason: Single issue but with very detailed root cause analysis pinpointing the code path (record_context_updates_and_set_reference_context_item skips build_initial_context on resumed threads). Workflow-blocking: users relying on implicit skill triggering after resuming old threads will have broken experience. The feature was recently added (#12227, #10478) making this a clear regression.

source_issues.title: Resumed threads keep stale model-visible skills after new skills are added
source_issues.evidence: Detailed root cause analysis provided: resumed threads reconstruct a non-None reference_context_item, which skips build_initial_context() and only emits settings diffs, leaving the model-visible ## Skills section stale. New skills missing from model-visible inventory; implicit triggering does not pick up new skills. Explicit $skill-name still works, and UI skill list updates — but the model context is stuck.

signals.topic: Thread history and all subagent threads lost after Codex App restart
signals.summary: When the Codex desktop app restarts (e.g., after being prompted for system permissions), previously active threads revert to an earlier state and all subagent thread history is permanently lost. The issue is reproducible — reopening the app consistently shows missing thread messages and subagents.
signals.review_reason: Significant session state loss — threads and subagent history permanently lost after a normal app restart. This is a data integrity failure for the core session model. Even with count=1, the impact is severe (irreversible data loss) and the repro is straightforward.

source_issues.title: Lost part of thread history and all subagent thread history after Codex App restart
source_issues.evidence: After app restart, thread reverted to a couple messages previously with all sub-agent threads lost (across other sessions too). Issue is reproducible — user continues to reopen the app to missing threads and thread message history. Thread ID provided: 019d4f15-8541-7c83-85d0-4fc9abb8139b.

signals.topic: VS Code Codex extension experiences repeated stream disconnections interrupting active work
signals.summary: VS Code extension users experience repeated 'Stream Disconnected' errors during active sessions, preventing work from continuing. Affects the IDE integration path which is a primary usage surface.
signals.review_reason: Stream disconnection interrupts the IDE workflow which is a primary usage surface. While count=1, the 'cannot continue work' language indicates workflow blockage. Lower confidence because the issue description is brief.

source_issues.title: Stream Disconnected
source_issues.evidence: VS Code extension user reports 'repeated stream disconnected. Can't continue work.' Thread ID provided: 019d4cc0-c398-7562-9802-1934d6b3b945.

signals.topic: Session API lacks offset parameter for pagination and user-scoped session management
signals.summary: The get_items() method in SessionABC only supports limit-based truncation (returns latest N items). There is no offset parameter for pagination, and no built-in agent_users table to associate sessions with application users. This forces developers to implement their own user-session mapping layer, making it difficult to build multi-user chat UIs with standard pagination patterns.
signals.review_reason: Both issues are feature gaps in the session management layer. They do not cause crashes but are blocking for production multi-user applications requiring pagination or user-scoped session management. Combined count of 2 with clear production use cases (chat UIs, multi-tenant apps) warrants P2 priority. These are not bugs but missing abstractions that force duplicate work across every production deployment.

source_issues.title: Feature request: add offset parameter to get_items() for real pagination
source_issues.evidence: User states: 'Currently, get_items(limit=N) only supports truncation — it returns the latest N items. There is no way to paginate through a session history. This makes it impossible to efficiently browse or display conversation history in pages.' Use cases cited: chat UIs with 'load more', exporting history in batches, infinite scroll.

source_issues.title: Feature request: agent_users table to associate sessions with users
source_issues.evidence: User states: 'Currently agent_sessions exist independently without a way to associate them with application-level users. When building multi-user applications, there's no built-in mechanism to link a session to a specific user identity.' Cited Google ADK as reference implementation with User -> Session relationship.

signals.topic: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
signals.summary: When using the Agents SDK with prompt caching enabled, adding a base64-encoded file input causes the cache hit rate to drop from ~97% to 0%, even though the prompt prefix, instructions, and tool definitions remain unchanged. Repeating the same file restores ~90% cache, but mixing file and text inputs breaks cache routing for text requests.
aliases: prompt cache hit rate drops to zero with file inputs
base64 file input breaks prompt caching
signals.review_reason: Cache hit dropping to 0% with file inputs causes direct cost loss on every mixed-input request in production. This is not a low-level bug but a visible, measurable degradation of a cost-saving feature. Multiple rounds with consistent reproduction and active discussion confirm real user impact.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
source_issues.evidence: In production testing, adding a single base64-encoded PDF file input causes cache hit to drop from 96.7% to 0.0% across multiple rounds, then text-only requests also show 0% cache. Observed with gpt-5.4-mini, conversation store, prompt_cache_key, and previous_response_id chaining enabled. Cache only recovers when repeating the exact same file.

signals.topic: Tool preambles/commentary not emitted when structured output (output_type) is enabled
signals.summary: When using structured output via output_type parameter, tool preambles (user-visible messages before tool calls) are completely suppressed. The model jumps straight from reasoning to tool_calls, leaving a 'dead zone' with no user feedback during tool execution. Removing output_type restores preamble/commentary phase correctly.
signals.review_reason: Loss of pre-tool-call messages significantly degrades perceived latency and user experience in streaming agent workflows. The user provides a clear, reproducible test case and identifies this as a critical UX gap for production deployments. The fix would require either SDK-level or API-level changes, confirming it is a real gap rather than misuse.

source_issues.title: Preambles with structured output
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'Preambles are critical for reducing perceived latency — users see an immediate acknowledgment before the tool executes. Without preambles, there's a noticeable dead zone where nothing is streamed to the user while the tool runs.' Reproducible with output_type set vs unset.

signals.topic: AnyLLMModel corrupts reasoning deltas and fails validation in multi-turn tool call scenarios
signals.summary: AnyLLMModel has two related bugs affecting multi-turn conversations with tool calls: (1) vLLM reasoning deltas are corrupted by premature iterable flattening of Pydantic Reasoning objects, producing garbled output like 'content用户' instead of the correct reasoning text; (2) ResponsesParams validation fails when input transitions from str to list[TResponseInputItem] after multiple dialogue rounds.
aliases: AnyLLMModel validation error in multi-round conversations
signals.review_reason: Both issues are confirmed bugs with explicit code-level root causes and working workarounds. They block multi-turn agent workflows when using OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoints or any-llm providers, directly affecting the core agent loop. Multiple reproducible examples and two separate but related bug reports confirm this is a systemic AnyLLMModel extension issue.

source_issues.title: AnyLLMModel corrupts vLLM reasoning deltas by flattening iterable Reasoning objects too early
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro provided: _extract_any_llm_reasoning_text(delta) returns 'content用户' instead of '用户' when delta.reasoning is a Reasoning Pydantic object. Root cause identified in _flatten_any_llm_reasoning_value() checking Iterable before object attributes.

source_issues.title: AnyLLMModel failed ResponsePalms validation during multiple rounds of tool calls
source_issues.evidence: User provides a complete subclass fix: _make_any_llm_responses_params forces _AnyLLMResponsesParamsShim to bypass pydantic validation, directly passing payload. Root cause: any-llm's ResponsesParams.input field only accepts str, but after multiple rounds it becomes list[TResponseInputItem].

signals.topic: Responses WebSocket connection closes with code 1000 when temperature is a decimal value
signals.summary: When using the Responses WebSocket API (/v1/responses) with a decimal temperature value (e.g., 1.2), the WebSocket connection immediately closes with code 1000 and no events, causing the main API flow to fail silently. Integer temperature values work correctly.
aliases: Responses WebSocket closes on decimal temperature
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed functional bug that blocks the main Responses WebSocket flow. The WebSocket terminates with code 1000 and zero events when a decimal temperature is provided, meaning the API call fails silently with no error event and no completion. Users have provided a minimal reproducible script. Although count=1, the blocking nature (main flow fails with no error feedback) and the clear reproduction path justify P1. The library's validation of temperature as numeric is inconsistent — docs say numeric but decimals cause silent connection drop.

source_issues.title: Responses WebSocket (/v1/responses) closes with code 1000 and no events when temperature is a decimal (e.g., 1.2)
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with minimal reproduction script. User calls wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses with temperature: 1.2, connection closes with code 1000 and empty event list. Same call with temperature: 1 works. This blocks the main Responses WebSocket flow entirely — no completion events are emitted and the connection terminates prematurely.

signals.topic: HTTP client throws unhandled InternalServerError (502) when calling local LLM servers on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows, calling a local LLM server (e.g., LM Studio at 127.0.0.1:1234) via the OpenAI Python client results in an unhandled InternalServerError with HTTP 502, blocking local LLM integration workflows.
signals.review_reason: Single occurrence but presents a concrete blocking scenario: the library throws unhandled InternalServerError on HTTP 502 from a local LLM server, with a full stack trace showing the error originates in _base_client.py. The error is not gracefully handled, which could indicate the library does not properly handle 502 responses from proxy/local LLM servers. Since count=1 and it's a specific local server scenario (may be LM Studio server-side), priority is P2.

source_issues.title: windows call lmstudio (127.0.0.1:1234/v1), get 502
source_issues.evidence: Bug report from Windows user with full stack trace. User calls a local LM Studio server (127.0.0.1:1234/v1/chat/completions) via the official Python client (v2.30.0), and receives openai.InternalServerError with HTTP 502. The traceback shows the error is thrown from _make_status_error_from_response in _base_client.py, meaning the library does not gracefully handle 502 responses from local LLM proxy servers. This blocks local LLM integration workflows on Windows.

signals.topic: Windows + Node.js v22: spawn EINVAL causes all agent commands to fail
signals.summary: On Windows with Node.js v22.12+, child_process.spawn() returns EINVAL when executing .cmd/.ps1 wrapper scripts (npx, node, npm-installed CLIs) without shell:true. This makes all agent commands (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Gemini) completely non-functional. The only workarounds are HTTP API mode or downgrading to Node.js v20.
aliases: Node.js v22 Windows agent spawn failure
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 despite count=1 because it completely blocks the primary workflow (running agent commands) for 100% of Windows users on Node.js v22 — arguably the most common modern Windows Node setup. All built-in agent commands are broken. The user impact is total functional loss with no acceptable workaround other than env downgrade. The severity and breadth of impact meet P0 criteria even at count=1.

source_issues.title: Bug: spawn EINVAL on Windows with Node.js v22 — all agent commands fail
source_issues.evidence: All agent commands fail with EINVAL on Windows Node.js v22. Zero agent commands work (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Gemini — all use .cmd/.ps1 wrappers). Workaround: HTTP API mode or downgrade Node.js to v20.

signals.topic: macOS: persistent sessions immediately report dead with 'queue owner unavailable'
signals.summary: On macOS, persistent acpx sessions are created successfully but immediately report 'dead / queue owner unavailable' on status checks. This breaks OpenClaw ACP thread-bound persistent sessions entirely, forcing users to fall back to one-shot mode. The root cause may be a queue owner process exit race or incorrect health probing.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the persistent session feature — a key workflow feature — on macOS, forcing users into a degraded one-shot-only mode. While count=1, the impact is a core feature (persistent sessions/thread-bound workflows) becoming entirely unusable, which qualifies as significant UX degradation.

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions become dead immediately (queue owner unavailable) on macOS
source_issues.evidence: Persistent sessions created successfully on macOS immediately report 'dead / queue owner unavailable'. Thread-bound ACP sessions are unstable. Workaround: use ACP in one-shot mode only (mode: 'run', thread: false). Downstream OpenClaw logs confirm 'acpx ensureSession replacing dead named session'.

signals.topic: parseAgents() silently ignores 'args' field in agent config, causing agent startup to hang
signals.summary: The 'args' field in ~/.acpx/config.json agent configuration is silently ignored by parseAgents(). This causes custom agent commands that require arguments (e.g., Cursor CLI with 'agent acp') to start without the correct subcommand, leading to ACP protocol initialization hanging. The config schema documents 'args' as supported but it has no effect at runtime.
signals.review_reason: Agent commands with args silently fail and hang, which is a genuine UX pain point — users configure agents expecting them to work, but the args are silently dropped. However, count=1 and there is a documented workaround (put all args in the command string), so it does not rise to P1.

source_issues.title: fix: parseAgents() ignores 'args' field in ~/.acpx/config.json agents config
source_issues.evidence: The 'args' array in agent config is silently ignored. Agent process starts but without the correct subcommand, causing ACP protocol initialization to hang. Reproduced across acpx versions 0.3.1, 0.4.0, and latest main.

signals.topic: No bulk-delete or prune command for closed sessions, leading to disk accumulation
signals.summary: acpx sessions close only marks sessions as [closed] in the list without deleting files, causing orphaned session files to accumulate (up to 2.4GB in one reported case). Users must manually delete session files to reclaim disk space.
aliases: no prune command for closed sessions
signals.review_reason: While disk accumulation (2.4GB) represents a real cost/UX degradation, the issue is fundamentally a feature request for a bulk-delete command rather than an existing failure that blocks or breaks a workflow. It does not prevent sessions from being used; it only accumulates unused files over time. Count=1 also argues for P2.

source_issues.title: Feature: command to bulk-delete closed sessions
source_issues.evidence: No bulk-delete or prune command exists. Sessions close does not delete files. Orphaned session files accumulate (reported: 190 closed sessions = ~2.4GB). Manual file deletion is the only cleanup method.

signals.topic: Security scanner generates excessive false positives, blocking legitimate skills from installation
signals.summary: Multiple developers report their benign skills (email clients, payment tools, fitness trackers, local dev tools, financial advisors, media tools) being flagged as 'suspicious', with no clear explanation of trigger patterns, causing repeated appeals and installation failures for end users.
aliases: Legitimate skills blocked by suspicious-pattern detection
signals.review_reason: This is a P0 pain point: 10 distinct developers across diverse legitimate use cases (email, payments, fitness, local dev tools, media, finance) all report their benign skills being blocked by the security scanner. The volume (10/21 non-spam issues), diversity of affected skills, and direct user impact (skills cannot be installed by end users) make this a primary platform-level defect. Multiple developers explicitly note that VirusTotal finds nothing wrong, confirming the scanner is the root cause.

source_issues.title: Skill flagged that needs to be remove
source_issues.evidence: Skill for ffmpeg/Gradio/qwentts flagged as suspicious; VirusTotal confirms safe; developer is a first-time skill creator unable to publish

source_issues.title: [Appeal] Skill flagged suspicious: clevrpay
source_issues.evidence: Legitimate payment integration skill flagged; developer made changes to address all known triggers but flag persists

source_issues.title: Coinw Contract Skill and Coinw Spot Skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Legitimate exchange connector skills (similar to Binance Pro) incorrectly flagged; developer asks what to fix

source_issues.title: email-suite (imap+smtp) - False positive: env var + network send is legitimate IMAP/SMTP auth
source_issues.evidence: Email client skill flagged for 'env var + network send'; this is the standard IMAP/SMTP auth pattern; requests exception for email/SSH clients

source_issues.title: [False Positive Appeal] Skill Fa.Pro-融资顾问 Incorrectly Flagged as Suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Legitimate financing advisor skill flagged; developer speculates flag is triggered by WeChat contact, Pro version label, or data/ directory

source_issues.title: local-rag deemed suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Local RAG skill for PDF processing flagged without explanation; developer has no idea why

source_issues.title: onelap-sync-strava flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Strava sync skill flagged; VirusTotal confirms no security vendors flagged file as malicious

source_issues.title: [Security Flag Review] 动画视频制作skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Animation video skill flagged despite scan details describing it as coherent and benign; page shows Benign with high confidence yet flag persists

source_issues.title: Appeal: mocklab skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Local API mock server for dev/testing flagged; developer provides detailed explanations for each flagged pattern (CORS=*, state_store.json, mock phone/idcard fields, uvicorn 0.0.0.0)

source_issues.title: Skill flagged suspicious: clevrpay
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate appeal for clevrpay; closed then re-opened as 1476; indicates no resolution path

signals.topic: No CLI mechanism to filter or inspect security status before skill installation
signals.summary: Users installing packages via CLI cannot see or filter by security status, leading to repeated failed installs of non-benign packages and forcing manual security checks through the web UI before each installation.
aliases: Cannot filter by benign-only in CLI install
CLI lacks security status visibility during package install
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow friction pain point: the user explicitly describes a broken install flow where 70% of packages are non-benign and cannot be filtered from the CLI, forcing manual web-based security checks. While count=1, the described impact is significant (repeated install failures, broken automation) and the request is actionable (CLI filter for benign packages). Kept as P1 due to count=1.

source_issues.title: Allow to view security from CLI
source_issues.evidence: User reports ~70% of packages are not Benign; no way to filter or inspect security status from CLI during 'claw install package'; user must manually check web UI before each install

signals.topic: Security scan results are inconsistent between web UI and mobile app for the same skill
signals.summary: The same skill shows 'Benign — high confidence' on the ClawHub web page but displays a 'This skill has been flagged as suspicious' banner in the mobile app, causing user confusion and trust erosion in the security system.
aliases: Web and mobile app show conflicting security statuses
Mobile app scanner disagrees with web scanner
signals.review_reason: This is an edge case affecting a single skill, but the root cause (inconsistent scanner results across platforms for the same artifact) is a systemic reliability issue. Kept as P2 since only one confirmed instance but the inconsistency undermines trust in the entire security system and could affect any skill.

source_issues.title: False positive: ichendong/cpbl flagged as suspicious (mobile app)
source_issues.evidence: CPBL skill shows Benign high confidence on web but suspicious banner in mobile app; developer speculates CSRF token caching or headless browser triggers scanner differently; user cannot trust either interface

signals.topic: Skill security flag triggers account lockout, blocking developer from publishing or managing skills
signals.summary: When a skill is flagged as suspicious, the developer's account is locked (401 Unauthorized), preventing all publishing, updating, and management of skills until the flag is resolved — creating a hostage situation for legitimate developers.
aliases: API token invalidated following suspicious-pattern flag
Developer access revoked when skill is flagged
signals.review_reason: This is a severe developer-experience pain point: account lockout following a suspicious flag creates a hostage dynamic where developers cannot even appeal or fix their skills. While count=1, the impact (full account lockout, blocks publishing of all skills including unrelated ones) is severe. Kept as P1; would be P0 if corroborated by additional instances.

source_issues.title: [Appeal] Account clawgrid locked after skill flagged — requesting account restoration
source_issues.evidence: Developer published clawgrid-connector skill; skill was flagged; API token immediately started returning 401 Unauthorized; developer completely locked out of account, unable to publish updates or manage any skills

signals.topic: Suspicious-pattern flag persists even after skill reaches Benign rating with no user actionable path
signals.summary: Developers who fix flagged patterns and achieve a Benign rating still see the 'Skill flagged — suspicious patterns detected' banner, with no explanation of what remains flagged or how to resolve it.
aliases: Benign status and suspicious flag coexist
No actionable feedback after reaching benign rating
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking pain point: the developer followed the full remediation path (fixed all flagged patterns → benign rating) yet is still blocked by a persistent flag with no actionable feedback. This creates a dead-end where the developer cannot resolve the issue independently, blocking skill publication.

source_issues.title: Why is my skill flagged as suspicious even after reaching benign status?
source_issues.evidence: Developer fixed all flagged patterns one by one until skill reached benign rating; a separate banner still shows 'Skill flagged — suspicious patterns detected' with no details on what remains flagged or how to fix it; developer cannot proceed

signals.topic: Client fails to send messages due to missing scope permissions
signals.summary: Users cannot send messages because the client lacks the required operator.write scope. Even the demo quick-send feature fails.
signals.review_reason: Main flow completely blocked — users cannot send messages at all. Even the demo quick-send fails. Clear cost loss as core messaging functionality is unavailable.

source_issues.title: I developed a client to send messages to openclaw, but it consistently fails to send. Even using the demo's quick send feature also fails to work
source_issues.evidence: [WARN] Gateway request failed: missing scope: operator.write

signals.topic: SSH tunnel not restarted on unexpected process exit
signals.summary: When the SSH tunnel process crashes, remote connectivity breaks permanently until manual user intervention.
aliases: Remote connectivity breaks after tunnel exit
signals.review_reason: Remote connectivity becomes completely unavailable after tunnel crash. User must manually intervene to restore. Blocking for users relying on SSH tunnel functionality.

source_issues.title: Bug: SSH tunnel not restarted on unexpected exit
source_issues.evidence: If the SSH tunnel crashes, the entire remote connectivity feature is broken until the user manually intervenes (e.g., changes settings or restarts the app). The reconnect loop will spin forever against a dead localhost port.

signals.topic: Signature mode fallback does not retry connect message — client stays stuck in Connecting state
signals.summary: Client permanently gets stuck in Connecting state when the initial signature mode is rejected, with no automatic recovery.
signals.review_reason: Client permanently stuck in Connecting state when signature mode is rejected. WebSocket open but unauthenticated. Main flow blocking for affected users.

source_issues.title: Bug: Signature mode fallback never retries connect message
source_issues.evidence: Client gets permanently stuck if the initial signature mode is rejected. The advanced mode only takes effect if the connection drops and a full reconnect cycle happens, which may not occur.

signals.topic: Node mode shows as Disconnected despite successful gateway connection
signals.summary: The node connects to the gateway but device pairing never reaches the server, leaving Node Mode stuck in Disconnected state.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (node mode / device pairing) does not work. Status shows Connected but Node Mode is Disconnected and no pairing request reaches server. Users cannot use node functionality.

source_issues.title: Node mode not work
source_issues.evidence: Status: Connected, Node Mode: Disconnected. On server side, no device pairing request found.

signals.topic: Overheight menu does not scroll vertically — menu items off-screen are inaccessible
signals.summary: When the system tray menu exceeds monitor height, no scrollbar appears, making bottom menu items unreachable.
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation — users cannot access menu items cut off at screen edges. Not main-flow blocking but a meaningful usability failure.

source_issues.title: Overheight menu doesn't scroll vertically
source_issues.evidence: If the menu is over-height for the monitor when the tray icon is clicked, no vertical scrollbar is shown to allow the user to access menu items which flow off the bottom of the screen.

signals.topic: URL/special-character content causes crashes or silent session drops across webchat and sessions.create API
signals.summary: Sending a localhost URL in webchat crashes the session with a grammy module error; sessions.create API silently drops any message containing '://' after 4.1 upgrade (no LLM call, no hooks fire); exec obfuscation detector false-positives on URL-like strings in quoted arguments
aliases: exec false positive on URL patterns
signals.review_reason: Three separate components all mishandle URL-like content: webchat crashes entirely on localhost URLs (channel unusable), sessions.create silently drops any URL after 4.1 (showstopper for any URL-processing workflow), and the exec detector false-positives on URL patterns inside quoted strings. The sessions.create issue is especially severe — it appears to succeed (status: started) but the agent never runs, making the failure invisible to users until they check the empty transcript.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Webchat crashes when user sends localhost URL in message
source_issues.evidence: Sending a localhost URL (e.g., http://localhost:8080/?state=...) in webchat causes OpenClaw to throw: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'grammy' imported from ...openclaw\dist\sticker-cache-BqQLBzvo.js; webchat becomes unusable; only workaround is using Feishu channel instead

source_issues.title: sessions.create silently drops messages containing :// (2026.4.1+)
source_issues.evidence: Any sessions.create message containing '://' (URLs, postgresql://, mysql://, mongodb:// connection strings) causes agent dispatch to silently fail; session is created with status 'started' but never runs — no hooks fire, no LLM call, transcript empty; works on 2026.3.28, broken on 2026.4.1 and 2026.4.2; showstopper for any workflow processing URLs or connection strings

source_issues.title: Exec Obfuscation Detector AI False Positives on Quoted String Arguments
source_issues.evidence: Exec obfuscation detector blocks legitimate commands when shell patterns like 'curl | bash' appear inside quoted string arguments to non-shell commands; command 'python3 inbox.py write tj nancy "Install Hermes" "Install command: curl -fsSL https://example.com/install.sh | bash"' is denied despite the pattern being inert inside a quoted Python string; forces workarounds like writing message bodies to temp files

signals.topic: WhatsApp TTS tool reports success but delivers no audio (silent failure) and subsequent messages receive stale/cached replies
signals.summary: On WhatsApp channel, the TTS tool claims success ('Generated audio reply.') but writes no file and delivers nothing; separately, consecutive inbound messages within ~90s receive identical cached replies in 5ms with no LLM call, meaning wrong content is delivered silently
aliases: WhatsApp stale cached reply dispatcher bug
signals.review_reason: Two distinct WhatsApp channel failures: (1) TTS silently delivers nothing despite claiming success — user has zero indication of failure and no way to diagnose it; (2) consecutive messages receive wrong/cached replies in 5ms, meaning the agent dispatches stale content without even invoking the LLM. Both are silent main-flow failures on a production messaging channel with no error output.

source_issues.title: Bug: TTS tool reports success but no audio file is generated or delivered on WhatsApp
source_issues.evidence: TTS tool returns 'Generated audio reply.' but no audio file is written to /tmp/openclaw/tts-*/ or any media directory; no audio sent to WhatsApp; no error in logs; workaround via sag CLI + message tool works — proving API key and WhatsApp send path are functional independently

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp web-auto-reply dispatches stale/cached reply to subsequent inbound message (5ms response, no LLM call)
source_issues.evidence: Second message within ~90s receives identical copy of first message's reply; second reply completes in 5ms (vs 597ms for first); different MessageSid values confirm inbound dedup works; bug is in outbound reply dispatcher buffer — wrong content silently delivered to user

signals.topic: Images bypass 5MB Anthropic limit — no auto-resize on OpenAI compat gateway or Slack channel
signals.summary: Image sanitization/resize pipeline is bypassed on the OpenAI-compatible gateway path (large Retina screenshots hit Anthropic 5MB limit; in streaming mode the error is completely swallowed), and Slack channel stores raw images that pass OpenClaw's 6MB check but fail Anthropic's 5MB limit
signals.review_reason: Two paths for image processing both fail silently on the same root cause (Anthropic 5MB limit vs OpenClaw 6MB threshold). Issue 59913 additionally loses errors in streaming mode, so users see no indication their image was rejected. Common scenario (Mac screenshots, Slack sharing) breaks by default for all users on those channels.

source_issues.title: OpenAI compat gateway images bypass sanitization/resize, hit Anthropic 5MB limit
source_issues.evidence: Images via OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions bypass image sanitization/resize; Mac Retina screenshots forwarded at full resolution and hit Anthropic's 5MB limit; in streaming mode the Anthropic API error is completely swallowed — client receives only 'data: [DONE]' with no error content

source_issues.title: Inbound images from Slack exceed Anthropic 5MB base64 limit (no auto-resize)
source_issues.evidence: Slack stores images raw (unlike Telegram which compresses); images of 5-6MB pass OpenClaw's MAX_IMAGE_BYTES (6MB) check but get rejected by Anthropic's 5MB limit; root cause: MAX_IMAGE_BYTES set to 6MB in src/media/constants.ts but Anthropic's limit is 5MB; affects all Slack image workflows with no workaround

signals.topic: Isolated cron/heartbeat sessions fail to inherit config — safeBins approval bypass ignored and bundled plugin module resolution broken
signals.summary: Cron jobs and heartbeat polls spawn isolated sessions that (1) do not inherit tools.exec.safeBins, causing exec commands to hang waiting for approval no human can give, and (2) fail to resolve bundled plugin modules (image-generation-core, telegram), causing cron jobs to crash at boot
aliases: Cron isolated session config not inherited
signals.review_reason: Both issues break automated cron/heartbeat sessions — the core use case for unattended operation. Issue 59908 causes cron jobs with exec to hang forever (no approval possible without a human); issue 59901 is a regression in 4.1 where cron jobs crash at boot entirely. Together they make scheduled automation unreliable or completely broken.

source_issues.title: tools.exec.safeBins not inherited by isolated cron/heartbeat sessions
source_issues.evidence: tools.exec.safeBins configured globally or per-agent is not propagated to isolated sessions from cron jobs or heartbeat polls; exec commands that should bypass approval still trigger the approval flow in sessions where no human is present — commands hang indefinitely or silently fail; breaks core automation that relies on safeBins for unattended execution

source_issues.title: [Bug]: 4.1: Unable to resolve bundled plugin error on image-generation-core/runtime-api.js and telegram module in cron jobs
source_issues.evidence: After clean install of openclaw@2026.4.1, cron jobs crash with module resolution errors: 'Unable to resolve bundled plugin public surface image-generation-core/runtime-api.js' and 'Cannot find module /usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/telegram-B2Tb4iqk.js'; files exist on disk but resolution fails in isolated cron sessions; multiple core automation jobs are broken at boot with no execution

signals.topic: OpenClaw stuck at loading screen after switching to Ollama/gemma4:26b model — agent becomes completely unusable
signals.summary: After downloading gemma4:26b and configuring openclaw with it, the UI gets stuck at 'wake up, my friend' loading indefinitely (15+ minutes). Direct `ollama run gemma4:26b hello` works in 5 seconds, proving Ollama itself is functional — the hang is entirely within OpenClaw's startup flow
signals.review_reason: Agent becomes completely unusable after switching to a specific Ollama model — the loading hang is indefinite and blocks all interaction. While count=1, the user impact is total (main flow completely blocked with no recovery path except reverting model choice), and the evidence is concrete: direct Ollama CLI works in 5s, OpenClaw hangs for 15+ minutes. This meets P0 criteria through explicit, severe user-blocking evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: openclaw stuck at loading after switching to Ollama/gemma4:26b (stuck at `Wake up my friend`)
source_issues.evidence: After downloading Gemma4:26b and configuring openclaw with it, openclaw gets stuck at 'wake up, my friend' and loads forever (waited 15min+); direct 'ollama run gemma4:26b hello there' returns an answer in 5 seconds, proving Ollama works; the hang is in OpenClaw's model initialization path; agent is completely unusable with no workaround other than switching back to a different model

signals.topic: Uncaught exceptions causing app crash during launch or main workflow
signals.summary: Aider crashes with uncaught exceptions (AttributeError, ModuleNotFoundError, ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) that prevent the app from starting or completing core operations. Root causes include dependency version mismatches (aiohttp, openai, litellm), unhandled litellm exception types, and unhandled Python stdlib edge cases (symlink loops, NoneType paths, glob patterns).
aliases: Dependency version mismatch causes uncaught exceptions
signals.review_reason: 10 distinct uncaught exception issues (count=10, 2 duplicates consolidated) spanning startup crashes and workflow crashes. All are verified real user reports with full stack traces showing aider crashes before or during core use. Root causes include: litellm exception type sync lag (PermissionDeniedError appears in 2 issues), aiohttp version incompatibility, openai package mismatch, pathlib edge cases on Windows/Linux, SSL cert misconfiguration, and git lock permission errors. Users cannot complete basic workflows.

source_issues.title: Uncaught AttributeError in __init__.py line 240
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: module aiohttp has no attribute ConnectionTimeoutError - app crashes on startup before any user interaction

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in scrape.py line 144
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright' - app crashes when user runs /web command with no error guidance

source_issues.title: Uncaught ValueError in exceptions.py line 71
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: PermissionDeniedError is in litellm but not in aider's exceptions list - app crashes during send_message on permission errors

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in <frozen importlib._bootstrap> line 1004
